articleTitle: MW Level 280 GHz 2nd Harmonic Coaxial Gyrotron Cavity with Variable Corrugation Depth
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The demand for high-power gyrotrons at frequencies above 200 GHz is increasing. This is anticipated to provoke a growing interest in harmonic high-power gyrotrons. Interacting with the second cyclotron har-monic facilitates a doubling of the output frequency in gyro-devices using the same magnet system. Since the coupling of the electron beam with TE modes becomes inherently weaker, with increasing harmonic number, a suitable method must be found to suppress fundamental modes. The use of impedance corrugated inserts in coaxial gyrotron cavities has been presented in this regard. In order to increase the output power while main-taining the ohmic wall loading on the inner conductor at continuous wave compatible levels, we have devised a technique that enhances the efficiency of suppressing fundamental modes by employing a tapered corrugation depth on the inner conductor. This approach also increases the range of stable operation of the gyrotron and reduces the susceptibility of the operation to electron beam quality.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on Frequency-Locking Bandwidth of a Novel Coaxial Line Injection Structure Based on S-Band Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In order to address the frequency locking issues of S-Band magnetron more effectively, and to facilitate the research on large-scale arraying of magnetron for microwave oven applications, with the ultimate goal of enhancing heating uniformity, we conducted a study focusing on frequency locking of S-Band magnetron. In this study, we employed coaxial line coupling to inject signals into the S-Band magnetron. Due to the non-cutoff property of coaxial lines, they can transmit electromagnetic waves at any frequency, making them highly suitable for investigating injection locking in S-Band magnetron. By varying the coupling port structure while injecting a power of 50W, we achieved a maximum injection locking bandwidth of 8MHz.

articleTitle: Industrial Qualification of the THALES TH1509U European 170 GHz 1 MW CW Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The progress of the European THALES TH1509U 170 GHz 1 MW CW industrial gyrotron program is presented in this report. The test results on the upgraded TH1509U and the compliance with main technical requirements are discussed.

articleTitle: Design of a novel conical cut frequency-taper for a K-band Ring Bar Slow Wave Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel type of frequency tapering for a Ring Bar Slow Wave Structure (RBSWS) is presented. The proposed conical cut structure works from 19.3 to 20.3 GHz, under an operating voltage and current of 19.8 kV and 0.3 A, respectively. Simulation results, carried out by CST Studio 2023, show that the introduction of the conical cut made it possible to increase the peak output power by a factor of 25–35 % with a maximum electronic efficiency of 15.3 %. The novel proposed conical cut allows to obtain an RBSWS structure with a higher maximum output power.

articleTitle: Adjoint Method and its Application to Helix TWT Design
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We outline the derivation and illustrate the application of adjoint equations to the problem of determining the effects of small changes of various design parameters on the output power and phase of a helix TWT. For example, using our formulation, we can compute the expected change in gain due to small changes in beam voltage, current, or radius, and/or circuit phase velocity, Pierce impedance, and/or attenuation profiles. Such calculations are useful in determining required manufacturing tolerances, and may also be used in derivative-based optimization algorithms like steepest descent. The important feature of this method is that, once the adjoint solutions are obtained (by running just two simulations with particular initial conditions), they may be used over and over again to evaluate the effects of any perturbation or combination of perturbations of the design parameters without running any additional simulations. The adjoint solutions therefore serve as a type of Green's function for derivatives of the TWT output with respect to design parameters. The method applies both to small and large signal operation.

articleTitle: A Planar GaN Nano Air Channel Diode with High Current and Radiation-Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Nano air channel transistors have attracted significant attention over the past decade due to their remarkable characteristics such as high frequency and robustness in harsh environments. With low electron affinity potential and a high breakdown field, GaN is an excellent field emission material. In this study, we proposed a planar GaN nano air channel diode with a tip-edge structure created by focused ion beam technology. The device achieves outstanding field emission performance with an output current of 129μA and a low turn-on voltage of 0.2 V. Notably, the device retains its exceptional performance even after undergoing 400 cycles of testing and exposure to fast neutron radiation.

articleTitle: Wideband Glide-Symmetric Double Corrugated Gap Waveguide Traveling-Wave Tube for Millimeter-waves
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We investigate the application of glide symmetry (GS) and electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) technology in a glide-symmetric double corrugated gap waveguide (GSDC-GW) slow-wave structure (SWS) designed for traveling wave tube (TWT) applications. This structure offers the notable advantage of providing wideband operation while eliminating the need for a conductive connection between the top and bottom waveguide plates. Also, the backward wave does not have longitudinal field component. This study positions the GSDC-EBG structure as a promising candidate among SWS topologies for TWTs operating under similar conditions.

articleTitle: Field Emission Performance of Carbon Nanotube Emitters Fabricated with Varying Geometries
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have been a subject of considerable interest as field emission cathodes because of their unique field-enhancing structure. In this study, an automated experiment and electron beam diode were developed to provide precise and repeatable DC measurements of the CNT emitter current. This has enabled an accurate characterization of the DC performance of CNT emitters with varying geometries and growth parameters. Geometries studied include dense CNT forests with varying heights as well as photolithography patterned emitters. Emission current, turn on field, and emission current performance over operating time were measured. The findings of this research aim to explore the viability of CNT emitters as a potential alternative to thermionic cathodes for use in high powered RF systems.

articleTitle: A Survey of Advanced Features of the MICHELLE Beam Optics Simulation Code
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present advances, key features, and advanced capability in the MICHELLE charged particle beam optics code. Although the MICHELLE code was originally developed to support the vacuum electronics and accelerator physics communities, over the years it has had some significant developments that make it a truly general purpose charged particle beam optics code with many advanced models and features. This paper discusses some of the advanced models and features that we find useful in modern design and optimization workflow. These include capability for multi-faceted meshing (2D, 3D, unstructured, structured-multiblock, hybrid, all element shapes), various solution algorithms (steady-state, time-domain, Boltzmann electron, circuit model), latest advances in emission physics (generalized thermionic, general thermal-field with self-consistent heating effects, photoemission, secondary emission), thermal beam models, adjoint analysis integration, multi-physics analysis environments (CAD, meshing, solution, post-processing, pipelining, optimization, sensitivity), inter-code operability within user workflows, resolving highly-disparate feature scales and sizes, and computer platform support (laptop-to-HPC). The paper highlights these models and features that have evolved over time and identifies cases where they can be applied to improve simulation fidelity or enable new problems to be approached.

articleTitle: Devil's Horn Electric Field to Solve Abnormal Gain of Sheet Beam Traveling Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We noticed abnormal gain behavior of the sheet beam traveling wave tube. Analysis shows that the difference in the interaction strength between the edge electrons and the central electrons of the sheet beam (SB) causes abnormal gain. It is proposed to use the devil's horn shape electric field to achieve a uniform sheet-like interaction domain to solve this problem. The 3-D particle-in-cell simulation results verify this solution.

articleTitle: A novel Method for Sorting of Electrons in Gyro-TWT Multistage Depressed Collectors
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A novel method of spatial separation of electrons with different initial energies in the helical electron beams of gyro-traveling wave tube (gyro-TWT), which is configured by the externally applied transverse magnetic fields, is presented. To demonstrate the method, an asymmetric two-stage depressed collector has been designed. The simulation shows that the application of this method can realize electronic classification effectively.

articleTitle: Modeling of Sever in Two-Stage Serpentine Waveguide Traveling Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We develop a model for calculating the small-signal gain of a multi-stage serpentine waveguide traveling wave tube (TWT) with one sever. The presented small-signal model is based on a generalization of the Pierce model, assuming one-dimensional electron flow along a dispersive slow-wave structure (SWS), accounting also for the space-charge effect. We compute the theoretical gain for multi-stage TWT and compare our calculated results with particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. The good agreement underscores the effectiveness of our analytical model for the sever in a serpentine waveguide TWT.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of a Sheet Beam Electron Gun for Traveling Wave Tube (TWT)
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper presents a electron gun model for obtaining the sheet beam characteristics for Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) applications. The design measure involves the careful consideration of the dimensions, aiming to enhance efficiency and performance. Furthermore, the magnets are strategically placed to enhance the electron beam trajectory, ensuring accurate beam positioning within the TWT. The optimized electron gun enhances performance and efficiency of the sheet beam.

articleTitle: Improved Step-Type Coupling in a Complex Sub-THz Gyrotron Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Mode selection in terahertz gyrotrons can be improved by using complex cavity resonators. They can satisfy the resonance condition for two modes with the same azimuthal but different radial indices. One common problem for such designs is the excitation of unwanted modes by the radial step between the two cavity sections. For large radial steps with coupling of modes with a difference in the radial index of An > 1 this problem becomes even more severe. We compare a complex cavity design with improved step-type converters with a cavity with a simple step.

articleTitle: Adaptive Mesh Refinement Strategy for Microwave Devices Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The adaptive mesh refinement(AMR) is important for simulation of macrowave devices. It contributes to obtaining more accurate results. When AMR is based on recovery type(RC), the refinement is limited to the characteristics of field distribution. This paper presents a AMR method based on residual type(RS). Based on the solved equation and the solution of each element, the posteriori error estimates can be used for refinement directly.

articleTitle: A Novel Transmission Simulator for Traveling-Wave Tube With Periodic Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The availability of computer memory resources is a crucial limiting factor in simulating the input/output systems of travelling-wave tubes (TWT). By employing the component array domain decomposition method (DDM) to simulate systems with periodic structures, it becomes possible to store only a single period's finite element model in memory. This methodology alleviates the need to store the entire finite element model of the periodic structure in memory, resulting in a substantial reduction in memory resource consumption during the simulation process. In this work, a novel transmission simulator by leveraging the DDM is proposed. This simulator is specifically designed for the analysis of input/output systems within TWT that exhibit periodic structures. The analysis results of the staggered double grating sheet beam TWT demonstrate that the novel simulator requires significantly less memory compared to other simulators, while maintaining the same level of calculation accuracy.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in the Accelerator Electromagnetic Code ACE3P
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present recent advances in the electromagnetic code ACE3P which allows functional capabilities in the modeling of accelerator structures, optical materials as well as RF sources. We show the recently developed nonlinear module which incorporates materials with nonlinear dielectric susceptibilities allowing for modeling harmonic generation and frequency conversion. We also show the ability to model Klystron input and output structures using self-consistent particle-in-cell (PIC) in the ACE3P suite.

articleTitle: Terahertz Backward Wave Oscillator based upon Dual-sheet-beam Sine Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A dual-sheet-beam sine waveguide (SWG) backward wave oscillator (BWO) operating in the terahertz frequency range is proposed. The slow-wave characteristics and transmission model of the dual-sheet-beam SWG slow-wave structure (SWS) are optimized through calculations. The results show that in the frequency range of 0.574 THz to 0. 757 THz, the reflection coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> is below −27 dB, and the transmission coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> exceeds −9.78 dB. Beam-wave interaction calculations for the dual-sheet-beam SWG BWO reveal an output power exceeding 1.32 W within the frequency range of 0.572 THz to 0.644 THz. At an operating voltage of 20 kV, the maximum output power is 3.58 W at the frequency of 0.572 THz.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Electron-Beam Sine Waveguide TWT Operating at 340 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A novel dual-electron-beam sine waveguide slow-wave structure (SWG SWS) for application in the millimeter-wave and terahertz-wave bands is proposed in this paper based on conventional SWG SWS. The novel structure features a larger interaction area and more electron-beam tunnels, allowing for a greater input of DC energy, resulting in a traveling-wave tube (TWT) with higher output power. The slow-wave characteristics and transmission properties of the novel structure were calculated, and the results indicate that the transmission coefficient S21 is greater than -8.63 dB, and the reflection is less than -20 dB within the frequency range of 330 GHz to 350 GHz. The beam-wave interaction simulation of this novel structure TWT was also calculated, achieving an output power of 28.8 W and a gain of 24.6 dB at 340 GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling Traveling-Wave Tube Distortion via Transfer Curve Fitting
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this study, an additional (third) parameter is added to the two-parameter Saleh formula for fitting a traveling-wave tube AM/AM (AM=amplitude modulation) curve. The newly added third parameter effectively acts to control the radius of curvature of the TWT saturation region and enables a much better fit to measured TWT data. This methodology allows a very simple and fast way to model the nonlinear behavior of a TWT with good accuracy up to 6 dB beyond saturation drive. Hence, it can be part of a digital linearization mechanism with artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities.

articleTitle: Effect of Self-Affine Surface Roughness on Space-Charge Limited Current
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We derive approximate solutions to space-charge limited current density (SCLCD) for one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) planar diode geometries. The SCLCD for a multidimensional diode is first expressed as a function of vacuum capacitance of the diode. The approximate solutions for SCLCD for a smooth anode and a rough cathode are derived assuming self-affine roughness scaling for the surface of the cathode. We show that SCLCD increases significantly for highly irregular surfaces characterized by a low roughness exponent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\alpha)$</tex>.

articleTitle: The Design of the Electron Optical System Based on the Sheet Electron Beam Matching Focusing Magnetic Field for a 340-GHz TWT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The electron optical system (EOS) is a key component for the development of the traveling wave tubes (TWTs). This paper introduces the design of an EOS for a 340-GHz TWT, which employs a sheet electron beam (SEB) with a 24-kV voltage and a 95-mA beam current. The target cross section size of the SEB is 0.05 mm * 0.285 mm of equivalent current density is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$848 \mathbf{A} / \mathbf{cm}^2$</tex>. To confine the SEB with such a high current density, a shielded sheet electron beam matching focusing magnetic (shielded SEB-MFM) system is used. The simulation indicates that this magnetic system can restrict this SEB well, and all particles can pass through the 40-mm tunnel without any interception.

articleTitle: Critical Analysis of Simulations with Large-signal Codes: Pros and Cons of Modeling with Reduced-Order Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present the comparative study of results of modeling of different VE amplifiers obtained by the TESLA-family of large-signal codes, which now include 2.5D and 1.5D algorithms. Recent introduction of the reduced order, 1.5D versions of the TESLA-family of codes, created link between fully 2D and 1D models and made it easier to analyze the pros and cons of the reduced-order modeling. We will demonstrate results of our analysis by using different types of VE amplifiers, including klystrons, Serpentine and Coupledcavity TWTs. Main emphasis will be made on high-gain and high-efficiency devices, which modeling becomes especially sensitive to taking into account the whole variety of 2d-effects, including use of more realistic electron beam models and radial dependence of the RF/DC fields across the beam and beam-tunnel. We also will try to include in our analysis comparisons with the results of 1D models, which represent the very low end of the reduced-order algorithms.

articleTitle: Study of a 94GHz Extended Interaction Amplifier Using Interlaced Staggered Resonant Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The extended interaction amplifier (EIA) has been extensively studied and applied in satellite communication systems for its numerous advantages. An extended interlaced staggered resonant cavity (EISRC) is proposed based on the staggered dual-vane slow wave structure. The high frequency characteristics, effective impedance (M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>R/Q) and beam-wave interaction characteristics have been investigated. A staggered dual-vane SWS is designed to cooperate with the EISRC. Combining the slow-wave structure (SWS) and multigap resonant cavities results in a complementary hybrid of traveling- wave and standing-wave elements, thus offering a broadband of input and output signal. The saturated output power of the EISRC is 229W at 94.06GHz, corresponding gain of 38.87dB, electronic efficiency of 3.96%, and the 3dB bandwidth is 93.9GHz to 94.1GHz. Compared with other EIK, the perspective of interaction length is shorter and the total periods decrease significantly.

articleTitle: The Effect of Thermal Contact Resistance on Space Helix Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: It mainly studies the contact thermal resistance between the helix and the clamping rod in the slow wave structure of a helical traveling wave tube. Firstly, starting from the single point contact model, a theoretical calculation model of contact is obtained, and the influence of contact thermal resistance on heat transfer in the slow wave structure is simulated using finite element analysis software. It is confirmed that contact thermal resistance does indeed hinder heat transfer, leading to temperature discontinuity. And based on the obtained temperature data, the numerical value of contact thermal resistance was calculated using theoretical formulas, and the influence of contact pressure and surface roughness on contact thermal resistance was analyzed

articleTitle: The Effect of Velocity Spread on a Ka-Band Large-Orbit Gyro-TWT with Periodic Dielectric-Loaded Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a gyro-TWT operating in the large-orbit electron beam mode, with the aim of reducing the working magnetic field while ensuring operational efficiency. The periodic dielectric-loaded structure, which has been successfully applied in the development of small-orbit devices, is adopted as the high-frequency interaction circuit. This tube works at second harmonic of electron frequency in the mode of large-orbit electron beam. The required magnetic field is only 5100 Gauss, which can be generated using electromagnetic coils instead of superconducting magnets. The paper presents the output power versus frequency under different velocity spread, within the velocity spread of 5%, good performance of the device can be achieved.

articleTitle: Design of Electron Optics System for D-Band Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper presents the design and verification of the electron optics system (EOS) for D-band Travelling Wave Tubes (TWTs). The electron gun generates a beam current of 57 mA at a beam voltage of 19000 V, with a beam waist radius of 0.068 mm and a shooting distance of 14.9 mm. To ensure stable focusing and transmission of the electron beam within the beam tunnel of 0.15 mm radius, a Periodic Permanent Magnet (PPM) focusing system with a magnetic field peak value of 0.52 T is utilized. Simulation results show that the fluctuation radius of the electron beam is less than 0.1 mm. The electron gun and PPM focusing system have been machined and assembled to validate the effectiveness of the electro-optics system of D-band TWT. Experimental results demonstrate that the emitted beam current is 49.83 mA and the collector current is 49.6 mA. Correspondingly, the beam transmission rate of 99.5% is achieved by carefully adjusting the PPM system.

articleTitle: Space Charge Limited Current Scaling for Short-Pulse Beam in a Vacuum Diode with Different Pulse Shapes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In applications where the pulse duration of an electron beam is shorter than the gap transit time, the Child-Langmuir (CL) law, describing the space-charge limited current density in planar vacuum diode, can be surpassed by a factor inversely proportional to the pulse length. In this study, we investigate the scaling of the current density limit as the pulse length decreases for square-top, trapezoidal, and Gaussian beam profiles using a 1D multiple-sheet model. Our analysis encompasses various factors contributing to the overall dynamics, including initial profiles, charge densities, and pulse widths.

articleTitle: Fabrication of W-Band Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier Beamstick Using Precision Alignment Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A W-band Serpentine waveguide Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) beamstick using elastic averaging, kinematic coupling and quasi-kinematic coupling precision mechanical alignment techniques was developed. Key components; electron gun, electron beam transport system and circuit each utilize a different alignment technique, leveraging their individual advantages for the specific component requirements.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Halbach Array and Periodic Permanent Magnet Circuit Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this paper, a performance comparison between two focusing systems, using a Periodic Permanent Magnet (PPM) and a Halbach Array (HA) for a circular beam Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) is reported. Magneto-static simulations demonstrate that HA is capable to generate the same magnetic field of the PPM configuration, with a reduction of the overall weight and radius of the magnetic circuit by a factor equal to 58% and 32%, respectively. These results pave the way for the exploitation of HA in circular beam-based TWTs and Klystrons for applications where weight reduction is fundamental.

articleTitle: Discussion on Mutual Coupling Phase-Locking Magnetrons
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This conference paper initiates a preliminary discussion on the mutual coupling phase-locking applied in magnetron arrays. Initially, we employed 4 and 8 magnetrons to investigate the feasibility of mutual coupling phase-locking technology in magnetron arrays. Additionally, we conducted research and analysis on the impact of the non-uniform emission capacity of magnetron cathodes on system performance. Simulation results indicate that the mutual coupling phase-locking scheme can be applied to multiple magnetron arrays, maintaining a consistently high phase-locking efficiency. Furthermore, the coherent synthesis efficiency of the arrays remains unaffected by differences in cathode emission capacity. The above work preliminarily demonstrates that mutual coupling phase-locking technology could be applied to achieve large-scale magnetron arrays for high-power applications.

articleTitle: Design of MIG for 250GHz, 50-100W Second Harmonic Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The design of magnetron injection gun (MIG) for 250GHz, second harmonic gyrotron oscillator excited at TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, 2 mode has been presented. The optimized MIG design is well-matched with 250GHz, second harmonic gyrotron oscillator, capable to deliver output power up to 50-100W. This electron beam source MIG, operates at a beam voltage of 20kV and beam current 61.5mA. The axial magnetic field ~4.5T is required for second harmonic operation. The MIG design has been optimized at beam compression ratio ~25 and a good quality of hollow electron beam and beam trajectory has been obtained with a low velocity spread 2.85% and velocity ratio ~1.44.

articleTitle: Design of a Precision W-Band Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present design and simulation progress on a W-Band TWT structure.

articleTitle: Miniature Sheet Beam Electron Gun
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We have developed a very small sheet beam gun that employs a 0.001-inch diameter tensioned tungsten wire cataphoretically coated with barium-strontium-calcium carbonate and capable of greater than 1 mA of emission current, see Fig. 1. The device includes a negative voltage hemi-cylindrical repeller electrode behind the cathode and a negative slit in front for suppression. Beyond the suppressor is a focus slit at cathode potential and, finally, an anode slit just beyond it. The repeller and slit electrodes provide effective collimation of the beam, which can be subsequently focused at narrow thickness either magnetically or electrostatically. A large number of these devices have been built and tested in sealed test vehicles. A common use is as ionizers for mass spectrometers in space. They have the advantage that they dissipate only 0.1 watt. The device construction will be described and performance presented. An alternative embodiment is the substitution of a 0.002-inch diameter thoriated tungsten wire. The emitting surface is actually smaller than the 0.001-inch wire with 0.001-thick barium oxide coating. The thoriated tungsten version allows multiple excursions to atmospheric pressures without loss of emission performance. However, it uses more power, about 0.6 watt vs. 0.1 watt. It easily produces a collimated beam of 5 mA at only 1450 degrees Cb. Its output can be raised to 10 A per centimeter squared at temperatures below 1700 degrees Cb.

articleTitle: Research on High-Power Microwave Synthesis and Transmission Based on Dichroic Plate in X-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: High-power microwave synthesis is a new technology that has been rapidly developing in recent years [1]. Researchers have recently focused on HPM multi-channel coupling as the main technical approach for power synthesis. Conventional multi-channel synthesizers, however, cannot operate in the over-mode waveguide state, which makes it difficult to sustain the continuous transmission of higher power energy.

articleTitle: Microstrip Meander-Line Slow Wave Structure with Ferrite Circulator for a Q-Band Traveling-Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this article, a novel microstrip meander-line (MML) slow-wave structure (SWS) with ferrite circulator for Q-band Traveling-wave Tubes (TWT) is proposed. Due to the magnetic anisotropy of ferrite, it exhibits gyromagnetic properties under a constant external magnetic field. This property allows the electromagnetic wave propagating through the ferrite circulator to have one-way transmission characteristics. For MML TWT with ferrite circulator it results in high reverse isolation and effectively reducing the power of reflected wave. Additionally, simulation results indicate that this new SWS can also increase the output power of TWT without cutting off the slow-wave circuit even without attenuator structure.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analogs of Emission and Breakdown on Cathode Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Understanding the processes associated with electron emission from cathodes is a key aspect in the development of future vacuum electronic devices, especially given that the drive for smaller, higher frequency devices is growing. This paper explores the use of electromagnetic analogs to model variations is electron emission due to atomistic surface effects on emitters.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Sensing and Communication in a Plasma Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: RF sensing and communication through a plasma channel poses severe challenges. Plasma blocks the transmission of RF signals below the plasma frequency, while electrically and chemically harsh plasma environment damages conventional electronics. In this talk, we will describe a new all-dielectric RF sensor based on a differentially-poled LiNbO3 micro resonator. This RF front-end, realized from a ferroelectric ceramic with high temperature resilience enables communication and sensing in harsh environments. Furthermore, the absence of metallic skin losses makes our approach ideal for THz applications beyond plasma cutoff frequency.

articleTitle: Design of a C-Band, High-Efficiency, Multi-Beam Klystron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Calabazas Creek Research, Inc. is developing a 5.8 GHz, 200 kW CW, multi-beam klystron (MBK) targeting an interaction efficiency of 80% or higher using recent klystron RF circuit design methods. While the “core oscillation method” (COM), the “bunch align collect”, and the “core stabilization methods” were investigated using the KlyC code, the COM design achieved the best performance. A hollow-beam approach resulted in an 84.1% simulated efficiency. When simulated in TESLA, the same RF design with adjusted external Q achieved 82.5% efficiency. For operation below 50 kV beam voltage and reasonable power density, a 6-beam MBK approach was chosen using coaxial cavities. Results from the RF cavity design (HFSS) and the beam optics design (BOA) will be presented.

articleTitle: Patternable On-Chip Waveguide Integrated CS3Sb Photocathodes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Integrated photonics, as an effective electron emitter, has the potential to pave the way for the next generation of photocathodes for accelerator applications. Here, we have demonstrated the feasibility of controlling light using waveguides and efficient material with a thin (<50 nm) film of photoemissive cesium antimonide. This integrated photonics cathode allows electron emission from specific sub-micron locations and precise temporal modulation. The approach results in the development of innovative photoemission mechanisms, i) enabling the unique shaping of emitted electrons and ii) beating patterns brought up from interference between two modes. This demonstrates the feasibility of integrating photonics into photocathodes, laying the foundation for converging photonics, nanofabrication, and photocathodes to create high-brightness electron sources for various accelerator applications.

articleTitle: An Electron Beam Manipulated by Laguerre-Gaussian Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Manipulation of electron beam by Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes is investigated using finite-difference time-domain particle-in-cell (FDTD-PIC) simulations. The simulated azimuthal velocity profiles of macro-particles display a 3-D spiral pattern with the number of strands equal to a sum of the state number of spin angular momentum (SAM) and the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of LG modes. These spiral patterns move along with the electron beam like a helical traveling wave. The macro-particles also exhibit both an orbit revolution and a small rotation motion. The former is very similar to the gyromotion of electrons under an external magnetic field. The rotation motion has the same frequency as that of the LG mode while the orbit revolution frequency is far lower.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel E-Plane Loaded Sine Waveguide for G-Band TWT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: To enhance the performance of the G-band traveling wave tube (TWT), a new slow wave structure (SWS) based on sine waveguide (SW) has been proposed, named E-plane loaded sine waveguide (EPLSW). Compared to SW-SWS, EPLSW-SWS exhibits higher interaction impedance and a significantly wider pass bandwidth for the same dispersion. Moreover, the numerical results have verified the broadband transmission characteristics of EPLSW- TWT in the G-band.

articleTitle: Thermal Emission Properties of a Hot Electron Laser Assisted Cathode
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We experimentally investigated the impact on electron emission of adding thermal energy to two types of Hot Electron Laser Assisted Cathodes (HELACs). We tested both types for evidence of theoretically predicted thermal-enhancement of photo-gated emission. We observed no thermal enhancement of photoemission on the first type due to lack of stability at elevated temperatures. Surprisingly, for the first type, we observed Richardson-Dushman-like thermionic emission consistent with a low work function material. This thermionic emission was weak or absent from the second type of HELAC. Our current investigations are focused on understanding the effective-low-work-function thermionic emission of the first HELAC type, while pursuing further experiments to confirm theoretical predictions that heating should enhance photo-gated emission for the second (more thermally stable) type of HELAC.

articleTitle: A User's Guide to Calculating Electron Emission
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The canonical equations of electron emission de- veloped in the early days of quantum mechanics relied on expedient approximations. Modern applications often rely on mixed conditions that compromise their accuracy. New equations indebted to a thorough reformulation have been rendered in a manner emphasizing the minimization of computational demands while preserving accuracy compared to the multi-dimensional integral emission equations from which they are derived. The development of accurate and rapid general thermal-field emission and three-step models are shown and numerical methods for their evaluation are demonstrated and contrasted to the canonical equations.

articleTitle: Development of X Band Pulsed TWT for Compact Synthetic Aperture Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A X band Helix Travelling Wave Tube (TWT), named ET6565, is being developed at Leonardo Palermo Plant under European Space Agency (ESA) contract n° 400012923219NLGLCvr., targeting a TWT for compact Synthetic Aperture Radar (cSAR) instrument, that is essential for Earth Observation. High power TWT is the key enabling technology for such SAR systems for Geostationary orbit (GEO), as well as Low Earth orbit (LEO) and Medium Earth orbit (MEO). Final objective of the current contract is to design, develop, and test a Helix TWT Engineering Model (EM) for LEO SAR with 4 kW peak RF output power, operating from 9 to 10,2 GHz at 10% duty cycle operating in relevant environment.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Double-Ridged Waveguide Diplexer with Evanescent Mode Coupling in L-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Miniaturization is one of the important development directions of vacuum electronic devices (VEDs) with the premise of high power. The double-ridged waveguide diplexer is presented in this paper with the characteristics of miniaturization and compact in L-band, which is used as an input structure for VEDs in dual-band operation. The reflection parameter is better than -20dB, and the transmission performance is better than 0.2dB in working band, while the isolation is better than 12dB.

articleTitle: Design of A Low Magnetic Field Coupler For Output Structure of The SLAC 75XP4 Klystron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Multi-megawatt X-Band klystrons use disk loaded traveling wave output structures for better rf power extraction efficiency. In this work, we have designed a new output coupler for the SLAC XP4 klystron operating at 11.424 GHz, which features an output cell with a fat-lip iris to reduce the surface magnetic field to safe levels. This design reduced peak pulsed surface heating below 500C at 75 MW output power and 2 µs pulse length, keeping the rest of the performance parameters of the cavity the same, i.e., the peak electric fields and peak modified Poynting vector.

articleTitle: Design Studies of a Three-Beam Metamaterial-Loaded Slow-Wave Structure for High-Power Microwave Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A metamaterial (MTM)-loaded, three-beam, all-metallic slow-wave structure (SWS) is presented. The proposed structure is comprised of periodically arranged split-ring resonator-pairs within a cylindrical waveguide, with azimuthal repetition at every 120°. The cold simulation and particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation analyses for the proposed metamaterial-loaded SWS are performed using CST simulation. Properties such as slow-wave propagation, negative group velocity, and below-cutoff backward-wave propagation are exhibited by the structure. The generation of output power of 140 MW at an operating frequency of 2.1 GHz within a pulse duration of 20 ns is confirmed by PIC simulation. Furthermore, an efficiency of 41% during this operational phase is demonstrated by the structure.

articleTitle: Study of Traveling Wave Waveguide Narrow Slot Array Antenna Based on High Power Capacity and High Radiation Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A traveling wave waveguide narrow slot array antenna (TWWNSAA) with high power capacity and high radiation efficiency is proposed for the arrayed phase locking magnetrons in terminals. The paper preliminarily explores the factors influencing the antenna's power capacity, namely the slot width (W) and radiation efficiency, of a single TWWNSAA. The simulation results show that: (1) the wider the slot width, the lower the radiation efficiency (within the usable range), and the higher the power capacity of the antenna. (2) For a center frequency of 2.458 GHz, with slot width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W=15mm$</tex> and radiation efficiencies of 80%, 85%, 90%, and 95%, respectively, the power capacities of the antenna in vacuum are 662 MW, 616 MW, 581 MW, and 544 MW respectively. The high-power microwave from the phase-locking magnetrons does not require a power combiner. Simply connecting each magnetron sequentially to each TWWNSAA allows for the efficient radiation of high-power microwaves of the same frequency and phase into free space. Therefore, it has great practical value in the field of high-power microwaves.

articleTitle: Analysis of Welding Residual Stress and Dielectric Loss Thermal Stress in High Power Output Window
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The output window of the high power Gyro-TWT is easy to be damaged, which is the key factor restricting the power and reliability of the Gyro-TWT. In order to achieve higher output power and reliability of the Gyro-TWT, the damage mechanism of the output window caused by the combined influence of welding residual stress and thermodynamic effects under operation must be considered. Establish an analytical model based on multiple physical fields such as elastic-plastic theory, thermodynamics, and electromagnetic theory. Three main nonlinear factors were taken into account: material nonlinear, geometric nonlinear and electromagnetic-thermo-solid coupling. The finite element method was used to analyze the distribution of residual stress and loss thermal stress in the output window welding. Some important phenomena have been found: welding residual stress of the high power output window is the compressive stress above 100Mpa. By combining nonlinear factors and the distribution characteristics of welding residual stress, the reduction of welding thickness can improve the redundancy of the power output window.

articleTitle: The Start-Oscillation Phase Condition for Backward-Wave Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The start-oscillation phase condition of backward-wave oscillators is believed to be 2πN, where N is an integer. This paper studies the hot-phase of circuit wave and space charge wave. As there is a discontinuity between the phase of the circuit wave and the space charge wave at the end of the tube, we conclude that the start-oscillation phase condition should be 2πN-3π/4, rather than the believed 2πN

articleTitle: Synthesis of Low-Hygroscopic Impregnant for Enhanced Reliability in Scandium-Containing Dispenser Cathodes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: To bolster the reliability of scandium-containing dispenser cathodes (SDCs), we utilized a co-precipitation method to craft a special composition impregnant engineered for robust stability in ambient air. Subsequent analysis affirmed its perovskite-like structure, showcasing enduring resilience in humid conditions without degradation. Furthermore, cathodes treated with this impregnation showed noteworthy low-temperature emission properties. This research lays the groundwork for enhancing the performance and longevity of SDCs, paving the way for their practical application in various devices.

articleTitle: From Single to Multiple Frequency Stability Analysis of VE Amplifiers Using TESLA-Z Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We report on ongoing efforts to develop a non-linear, multiple-frequency stability analysis framework based on the large-signal code TESLA-Z that is suitable for a large- signal stability analysis of Vacuum Electronic devices. This involves an extension of the previously developed linear “zero-drive”), single-frequency TESLA-Z based stability analysis framework, which was successfully validated by comparisons with experimental data and PIC code simulations. The approach combines a precomputed complex impedance matrix for the structure Z with a TESLA-Z computed admittance matrix Y of the beam-tunnel loaded with an electron beam. In the case of the large-signal stability analysis calculations of extended matrices will be made for the working frequency ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, as well as for the frequency ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> of an additional small-signal perturbation, which corresponds to potential instability. The extended gain matrix G for a given device then can be found as the product of the extended Z-matrix of the structure and extended admittance matrix Y of the beam-tunnel. Subsequent analysis of the eigenvalues of the extended gain-matrix G uses the Nyquist method to determine the stability of the device.

articleTitle: Investigation on Asynchronized Beams Electron Optics System
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A novel electron optics system is designed and simulated to support the project of “Forward and Backward Wave Feedback Circuit Terahertz Radiation”, which can emit, focus and transmit two different velocity electron beams with different shapes. The cylindrical electron beam with voltage of 16.38kV and current 0.013A and the annular electron beam with 5.7kV voltage and 0.013A current, which generated by the asynchronized electron gun, are injected into the interaction structure simultaneously. Furthermore, a uniform magnetic focusing structure, which constraining the beams with adjacent beam separation of 0.046 mm, can guarantee the transport stability in the interaction structure of 62.4mm. Simulation shows that the transmission of the dual-beam to 70 mm is 100% and the electron optics system meets the project requirements.

articleTitle: New Product Dual TWT THL 12070D and THL 12075D Qualification
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In the frame of new software defined satellites (SDS) using active antennas, Thales A VS is developing new traveling-wave tubes (TWT) for the Ku and Ka bands and named Dual TWT Referred as THL12070D and THL12075D, the two Ku designs have dedicated interfaces and are a breakthrough compared to heritage TWTs as they are composed of two RF lines on a single baseplate with integrated waveguides. Each line can have its own drive level despite several common HV cables. A deep work was conducted to compact all the sub-assemblies which results in a significant mass saving. The development phases and the designs being finalized, this paper describes their qualification.

Author Keywords: TWT / Ku band / Dual TWT / SDS / Active antenna

articleTitle: X-Band 20 and 25 MW Klystrons for High Pulse Repetition Rate Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The cost and sustainability of the large accelerator facilities are major concerns in the scientific field. Introducing the high-gradient accelerating structures at X-band frequency is an effective way to reduce the scale of the facility and cost. This is also beneficial for industrial machines in case its size is the matter. CETD (Canon Electron Tubes & Devices co., ltd.) have developed X-band 20-MW klystrons and a 25-MW klystron in these three years. The klystrons have the maximum pulse repetition rate of 400 pps, which meets the increasing needs for the operation of the linear accelerators at high repetition rate. In this report, the test results of the klystrons are presented.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Physics and Characteristics of Tunable Negative Electron Affinity Photocathode with High Quantum Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Negative electron affinity (NEA) photocathodes have long been pursued as an efficient electron source due to their enhanced quantum efficiency, narrow energy spread and high brightness or current density. Conventionally, NEA is achieved by applying a thin layer of cesium-rich oxide onto a semiconductor surface, rendering it highly reactive, unstable, and susceptible to environmental conditions [1]. In a recent investigation focused on electrostatically generated tunable NEA surface [2], an NEA photocathode is explored that exhibits remarkable stability in ambient conditions and allows for electronic tuning of its electron affinity. The present work discusses an enhanced iteration of this device, characterized by improved quantum efficiency and reliability.

articleTitle: Capacity of an Irregular Gyrotron Cavity to Provide an Increase in Output Power
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The maximum possible output power enabled by excitation of traveling-wave high-order axial modes of a cavity with irregularities for a second harmonic 527-GHz gyrotron is evaluated. The influence of mode conversion induced by cavity irregularities on gyrotron performance is investigated.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional calculation of axisymmetric coils and permanent-magnet system in MFS
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Magnetic focusing system usually adopts permanent magnet focusing system and electromagnetic focusing system(coil). To extend the function of MFS, the Magnet Field Solver of MTSS, which is mainly used for PPM system design, the magnetic vector potential method is studied and used to calculate the axisymmetric magnetic field of the magnetic focusing system including coil, permanent magnet and pole piece. The accuracy of the proposed method has been verified.

articleTitle: The Generation and Suppression of Monotron Oscillation in High-Power W-Band Extended Interaction Klystron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Monotron oscillation is a common problem in the design of high-power Extended Interaction Klystron (EIK), frequently leading to severe electron beam instability, thus disturbing normal RF power amplification. Therefore, this instability should be paid attention to and avoided in the early stages of design. In this paper, a method to avoid monotron oscillation by changing the cavity structure is reported and verified in PIC. The result shows that this method can effectively suppress the monotron oscillation in the multi-gap resonant cavity.

articleTitle: Multipactor in a Coaxial Geometry with Non-Sinusoidal RF Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We investigate multipactor in a coaxial geometry with non-sinusoidal Gaussian-type RF fields by employing 3D electromagnetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, ID analytical calculations, and statistical modeling. For different aspect ratios of a coaxial geometry, we analyze the effects of the RF amplitude and the full width at half maximum (and/or half minimum) (FWHM) on multipactor susceptibility and the time dependent physics. We find that with Gaussian-type RF operation, the threshold peak RF voltage as well as the threshold time averaged RF power per unit area for multipactor increases compared to that with sinusoidal RF operation. The effects of the Gaussian-type RF operation on the deposited power densities by multipacting particles on the inner and outer conductors are also analyzed.

articleTitle: Simulation of a Backward-wave Oscillator Operating at THz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this paper, a new Slow wave structure of double corrugated waveguide in slot is presented and applied to the design of back-wave oscillator. The double-corrugated waveguide slow-wave structure in the slot has the advantages of simple processing, low phase velocity, and high interaction impedance in the working area. Backward wave oscillators (BWOs) based on the double-corrugated waveguide slow-wave structure in the slot can achieve an output of more than 1W in the range of 282.3GHz-313.8 GHz at a voltage of 12.5 kV -25.5 kV.

articleTitle: Design and Thermal Analysis of a Coupled-By-Rods Interaction Structure for Traveling-Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The design and thermal performance of a coupled-by-rods interaction structure for coupled-cavity traveling-wave tubes (TWTs) is presented in this paper. The device features a new slot configuration consisting of a circular hole comprising of a metallic rod passing through it. This particular slot has been designed in order to allow a better thermal behavior, while maintaining comparable electrical performances to already known structures. The small dimension of the slot enables a more efficient heat dissipation, while the metallic rod ensures the magnetic coupling between the cavities. An X-band coupled cavity TWT making use of this new slot design has been simulated and compared to a conventional staggered slot structure. The coupled-by-rods structure has been capable of reaching a value of 13 kW of saturated output power, comparable to a conventional counterpart, and it exhibits a saturation temperature 75°C lower when compared to a conventional configuration.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Model of Transmission Lines Illuminated by HPM
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper proposes an equivalent circuit model (ECM) of transmission lines illuminated by high-power microwave (HPM). The electromagnetic coupling issue is transformed into a circuit problem by Thevenin's theorem, and the transfer impedance is fitted by vector fitting. The equivalent circuit method is more efficient than the full wave method with accurate calculation results, and calculation examples including linear and nonlinear loads verify the method.

articleTitle: Design of A High Efficiency Wide-Band 200W for Ku-Band Space TWT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A Wide-band Ku-band helix space travelling wave tube is designed in this paper. It is achieved by using the two-anode electron gun, the helix with pitch gradient technology and a High Efficiency five-stage multistage depressed collector. In the simulation results, output power is more than 230W,saturated gain is above 51.6dB and electronic efficiency is better than 35.1%. The collector efficiency exceed 83.13%. The total efficiency of the actual tube exceed 70.5%.

articleTitle: Carbon-Containing Cathodes: Field Emission and Structural Characteristics, Stability and Efficiency of Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Development and application of new electrovacuum devices using field emission effects for various fields of activity, for example: for disinfection, for creating a line of effective radiation sources of various spectral ranges and purposes, for electron guns of various powers, etc. are extremely relevant. Studies of various carbon-containing, including nanostructured, materials for field emission cathodes are of significant interest, since their electrical characteristics are closely related to the surface structure, which can change during emission processes and affect the efficiency and stability of field emission devices. In this work, field emission and structural characteristics of a number of carbon-containing field cathode materials, including nanostructured materials, were experimentally studied. As a result of measurements carried out using optical and electron microscopy, the presence of large-scale structural rearrangements of surfaces was shown, which manifest themselves under certain field emission modes during the operation of field cathodes for a number of carbon-containing materials. A comparative analysis of Raman spectra also showed small-scale structural rearrangements of surfaces for the materials studied. Based on the data obtained, estimates were made of changes in the sizes of carbon crystallites for a number of carbon-containing materials during their operation as field emission cathodes.

articleTitle: Reconfiguration and Millimeter-Wave Transmission Properties of Heat-Treated Self-Assembled Helices
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We characterize the effect of heat-treating helical slow-wave structures fabricated by self-assembly of Cr/Au/Cr nanomembrane ribbons. We observe that annealing introduces plastic deformation while reducing reflection and insertion loss in the helix. We attribute this effect to the annihilation of voids in the Au layer.

articleTitle: Characterization of Magnetron Cavity Loading Using Conformal Finite-Difference Time-Domain Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This work presents a comprehensive characterization of a magnetron cavity with loading, employing both conformal finite-difference time-domain (CFDTD) and finite element method (FEM) simulations. The focus of the investigation includes the derivation of the dispersion curve and a comparative evaluation of the loading effect, with specific emphasis on the load Q values obtained from both simulations. The dispersion curve provides critical insights into the electromagnetic wave propagation characteristics within the magnetron structure, facilitating a deeper understanding of the magnetron's performance. The comparative analysis sheds light on the advantages and limitations of each simulation method in predicting the Q value for various loading strengths. The results presented in this study contribute to the refinement and optimization of magnetron cavity designs, offering valuable insights into the electromagnetic characteristics and performance metrics. The integration of both CFDTD and FEM simulations enhances the accuracy and comprehensiveness of the cold test simulation analysis, paving the way for advancements in magnetron technology and microwave device engineering.

articleTitle: Permanent Magnet Solutions for Particle Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Some examples will be introduced to demonstrate the permanent magnet technology and its feasibility in the medical and scientific applications, where in general electromagnets have been used, in particular for particle accelerator applications. The quadrupole focusing magnets with an innovative field-adjustable feature and temperature compensator were designed and produced. The comprehensive design studies including magnetic and mechanical design using finite element analysis and iterative optimization were completed. Permanent magnet assemblies have been successfully built using rare earth magnets and the magnetic field measurement was conducted and compared with the numerical estimates. The effort was concentrated on the magnetic alignment, physical alignment, and field gradient error. This work suggests that the use of permanent magnet technology could result in manufacturing and operational cost reductions in accelerator applications.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Input Cavity of W-Band Extended Interaction Klystron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The Extended Interaction Klystron (EIK) amplifier is a high-power, high-frequency microwave device widely used in millimeter-wave band. Through the input cavity of an extended interaction klystron, the external microwave signal is introduced and the microwave electric field is established across the cavity gap, thus, the passing electron beam is modulated. This paper analyzes the key considerations in the cavity design of extended interaction klystrons, which encompass operating mode, synchronization condition, effective impedance and normalized electron beam conductance. Finally, a 9-gaps input cavity for W-band extended interaction klystron is designed and analyzed using CST Studio Suite.

articleTitle: TESLA-Family of Large-Signal Codes as Fast and Efficient Computational Tools for Accurate Modeling of Linear-Beam VE Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present an overview of the TESLA-family of large-signal codes, which now include klystron code TESLA, Coupled-cavity TWT code TESLA-CC, Serpentine/Folded-waveguide TWT code TESLA-FW and general-purpose code TESLA-Z. While the first 3 algorithms utilize classical circuit-based approach, the recently added into the family code TESLA-Z is based on impedance matrix Z importing and does represent more general, geometry-driven approach to the large-signal modeling. We will provide an overview and the current status of the TESLA-family of codes together with examples of their successful applications to the modeling of different types of linear-beam VE amplifiers.

articleTitle: Achieving Ultra-Wideband Slow-Wave Structure for High-Power Sheet Beam Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The emergence of sheet beam traveling wave tubes (SB-TWTs) in the millimeter-wave and terahertz has increased the operating power of traveling wave tubes (TWTs) by an order of magnitude. However, high-power SB-TWTs have been unable to achieve ultra-wide operating frequency range like helix TWTs. To break the bandwidth-limited of traditional SB-TWTs at high power operation, an innovative slow-wave structure (SWS) is proposed and verified as an effective solution for ultra-wideband high-power TWT in the millimeter-wave and terahertz. With the introduction of the side slots on both sides of staggered double-vane slow-wave structure (SDV-SWS), the circuit characteristics changed. While maintaining high power output, the operating bandwidth is greatly broadened. The ultra-wideband amplification characteristics have been verified through the particle in-cell (PIC) simulation at Ka-band.

Author Keywords: all-period phase velocity tapering optimization method

articleTitle: 3-D Folded Meander Line Slow Wave Structure for W-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper presents, a novel 3-D Folded Meander Line (FML) Slow Wave Structure (SWS) for W-band (70–110 GHz) applications of the traveling-wave tube (TWT) amplifier. The cold test analysis is performed using eigen mode solver of Computer Simulation Tool (CST) - Microwave Studio. The proposed structure consists of an extended path length thereby offering a flat normalized phase velocity with higher interaction impedance over the desired band. Furthermore, the effect of aspect ratio on dispersion characteristics is also thoroughly analyzed. In addition, a strong axial electric field (E-field) and a weaker magnetic field (H-field) ensure TM mode wave propagation. The simulated reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) is less than −10 dB in the W-band.

articleTitle: Latest Progress on the Development of Large-Signal Klystron Simulation Code KlyC
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: 1.5-D Large signal Klystron simulation code KlyC was initially developed for high efficiency (HE) Klystron projects since 2017, which could handle the design and optimization of mainstream pencil-beam (including multi-beam) Klystron projects. In recent 2 years, some new features to expand the functionality of KlyC has been implemented, to facilitate the analysis and development of novel category of Klystrons. In the up-to-date version of KlyC, traveling wave module is integrated to fulfill the SW/TW hybrid device development; Sheet electron beam (SEB) space charge model is supplemented to realize the SEB Klystron/TWT simulations. Small signal theory fully considering relativistic effects, cavity coupling, reflected electrons not only speed up the preliminary design of generic Klystrons (including broadband Klystrons), but also could be used to predict some sophisticated instabilities in high-gain Klystrons, such as those in Kladistron development. All these progress have been confirmed as both effective and accurate with rigorous benchmark with 3D particle-in-cell simulations.

articleTitle: Fabrication Precision of CNC-Machined Millimeter-Wave TWT Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present characterization of the precision and accuracy of millimeter-wave serpentine waveguide traveling-wave circuits fabricated by CNC machining. The critical dimensions of circuit piece parts were measured using a digital optical microscope. Measured results are compared across 10 duplicate fabricated circuits and the design model in order to characterize the repeatability and overall fabrication tolerances. Results are reported in relative units, normalized to the nominal mid-band operating frequency in the millimeter-wave range. We observe that the achieved precision of critical dimensions is close to the inherent limit of the CNC machine.

articleTitle: The 28 GHz / 35 GHz Dual Frequency Gyrotron System for Electron Bernstein Wave Heating and Current Drive in MAST Upgrade
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A 28 GHz / 35 GHz dual frequency gyrotron system has been designed and developed for electron Bernstein wave heating and current drive in MAST Upgrade. Stable power output ranging from 100 kW to 1 MW was confirmed, which is applicable to plasma heating experiments. After conditioning the gyrotron tube, we achieved 1 MW class oscillation power with a pulse length of 3 seconds at 35 GHz. This result is the world's highest performance for low frequency gyrotrons below 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Monolithic Fabrication of a Multiple-Electron-Beam Traveling-Wave Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present fabrication results and RF cold test of a multiple-electron-beam TWT circuit operating in the millimeter-wave frequency range. Due to the eight beam tunnels and helical waveguide geometry, the circuit is three-dimensional (3D) in nature and requires an additive manufacturing (AM) fabrication technique. The circuit was fabricated in a single piece using direct metal laser melting (DMLM) in Inconel 718 alloy.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on the Damage Effect of HPM on LNA
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper mainly introduces the damage effect experiment of high power microwave (HPM) on GaAs low noise amplifier (LNA). In HPW injection mode, the influence of high power continuous wave and pulses with different repetition rates on the damage threshold of LNAs was studied. The damage mechanism of LNAs was compared and analyzed, which provides an insight into the protection and reinforcement of LNAs.

articleTitle: Research on Peak Leakage Characteristics of PIN Diodes Limiters under High Power Microwave
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper adopts ADS to model and simulate a standard PIN limiter circuit, studying the effects of I layer thickness and different PRI pulse trains on the limiter's peak leakage characteristics, as well as the conditions for PIN limiters to produce peak leakage. When injecting a Ku-band pulse train with a pulse width of 100 ns and a PRI of 1 ms, the experiment verifies the peak leakage characteristics of the PIN limiter, which provides a way to improve the electromagnetic protection design of the PIN limiter.

articleTitle: Effects of Laser Pulse Length on Photoemission Spectra from a Biased Metal Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this study, we utilized an exact quantum model to investigate the emission of photoelectrons from a metallic surface subjected to a DC field and a femtosecond laser pulse. The impact of the laser pulse duration on the emitted photoelectron energy spectra is analyzed.

articleTitle: Low Temperature Leakage Sealing Technology for Vacuum Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Klystron as a typical vacuum electronic device has been widely used in the field of microwave devices. During the development of the klystron, leaks were generated due to factors such as process and material properties, resulting in losses due to the scrapping of the klystron. Au-Ge12 has been widely used as an excellent soldering material for material welding and metal encapsulation. In this paper, the ability of Au-Ge12 to repair leaks after klystron leakage is investigated with respect to its dispersion on oxygen-free copper and nickel-plated metal surfaces and the weldability of the two substrate materials. The experimental results show that Au-Ge12 has better dispersion on the nickel-plated surface; The dispersion is flatter on the oxygen-free copper surface with an average thickness of 78um; However, the welding properties of Au-Ge12 are worse, which can reduce the leakage rate to some extent.

articleTitle: Scaling of Crossed-Field Devices for High Power
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This abstract discusses the development of high power crossed-field devices through scaling a base design. Scaling rules will be discussed. Empirical results from several scalings of magnetrons and CFAs that achieved powers up to 20 MW will be presented.

articleTitle: Recent Progress of the G-Band TWT with Pencil Beam in BVERI
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The G-band pencil beam TWT amplifiers with high output power, high efficiency and significant bandwidth have been successfully developed in BVERI. The recent progress of TWTs is presented.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual Sheet Beam Electron Gun for THz Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The multiple sheet beam electron gun is an important part of multiple sheet beam devices. The design and simulation of a dual sheet beam electron gun for the THz traveling wave tube (TWT) are presented in this paper. Simulation results show that the dual sheet beam electron gun can generate a beam current of 2 × 0.34 A with a voltage of 29.3kV. Each sheet beam size of the beam waist is about 0.65 mm × 0.13 mm, which indicates a compression ratio of 7.9 and an aspect ratio of 5.

articleTitle: Study on High-Transmission Rate W-Band Electro-Optical System and Travelling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The electron beam is the “heart” of vacuum electronics device, providing energy for signal amplification.
