In this paper, we propose an electro-optical system (EOS), which provides an electron beam with high transmission rate for W-band traveling wave tube (TWT). Test results demonstrate that under the condition of a 21.6kV beam voltage, the electron gun can provide a 174mA beam current, and the beam transmission rate of short drift tube of EOS reaches 99.73%. To further validate the feasibility of the proposed scheme, a W-band folded waveguide TWT operating at 92-98GHz is designed based on this EOS. By adjusting the magnetic focusing system with the magnetic field value of 5300GS, the current transmission rate of TWT also reaches 99.7%, with a beam current of 161.4 mA at the beam voltage of 21.5kV. The output power of W-band TWT in the frequency band exceeds 100W, and the output power is higher than 150W in the range of 94-97GHz. The EOS has undergone comprehensive validation, laying the groundwork for the subsequent W-band continuous-wave TWT.

articleTitle: A High-Order Mode Terahertz Extended Interaction Oscillator with Three Electron Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: An effective high-order mode circuit is proposed for a terahertz extended interaction oscillator (EIO) with three electron beams. Compared to the conventional standard TM51 mode, the proposed quasi TM51 mode has five similar field spots distribution in the y-direction and higher characteristic impedance R/Q. The particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations showed that, operating at quasi TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">51</inf>-6π/54 mode with single electron beam, an output power of 2601 mW can be achieved at 612.15 GHz with a voltage of 28.3 kV and a current of 25 mA. When 3 electron beams are introduced, an enhanced output power of 3881 mW can be obtained at 612.51 GHz.

articleTitle: Operational Characteristics of the 330 GHz Continuous-Wave Clinotron with Modified Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The results of experimental studies of the clinotron tube with modified cavity operating in the frequency range 285-330 GHz have been presented and discussed. The maximum output power of 71 mW was measured for the accelerating voltage of 3.5 kV that corresponds to the operating frequency of 297.8 GHz; and the output power of 62 mW was detected at 329.4 GHz corresponding to the beam parameters of 4.5 kV and 150 mA. In the frequency range from 298 GHz to 315.7 GHz, there are several operating zones with an output power of 50 mW, while in the frequency ranges 285-295 GHz and 316-327 GHz the output power achieves slightly more than 25 mW.

articleTitle: Integrated Dark Current Radiation Study for Accelerator Structures Using ACE3P and Geant4
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A simulation workflow, ACE3P-G4, has been under development to study dark current (DC) radiation effects using ACE3P and Geant4. ACE3P-G4 interfaces particle data transfer and geometry between the electromagnetic (EM) cavity simulation code ACE3P and radiation code Geant4 and aims at solving large-scale problems using high performance computing. ACE3P-G4 starts with calculating the operating mode in the vacuum region of an accelerator structure and tracking field-emitted electrons under the influence of the EM fields of the mode using ACE3P, and then follows by particle data transfer at the vacuum-wall interface for subsequent radiation calculation in the wall enclosure materials using Geant4. This paper will demonstrate the ACE3P-G4 simulation workflow by performing large-scale dark current radiation calculations for the KEK 56-cell traveling-wave structure, and compare the simulation results with measurements at KEK. The efficiency of performing simulations on NERSC supercomputer Perlmutter will be presented.

articleTitle: Field Emission Radiation Source and X-Ray Tube for Analytical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper presents a promising design of an Xray tube with field emission cathode-modulator unit based on oxide emitter for soft X-ray radiation. Carbon in the form of graphite is used in “through-target” anode coating. Since oxide cathodes have been characterized by multi-peak energy spectra of emitted electrons, a digital model is proposed to simulate corresponding field emission electron-optical system taking into account appropriate initial-boundary conditions in the emission domain. Modification of cathodoluminescent UV radiation source is discussed by replacing the electron beam target, which inner surface coated by a luminophore.

articleTitle: Development of Extended Q-band 200W Helix TWT with Two Stage Collector
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Demand for Q-band satellite communications are increasing daily, utilizing high data rates and wide bandwidth. NEC Network and Sensor Systems, Inc. (NETS.) has developed a new high-power, wideband, Q-band TWT operating 200Wcw in the 42.5 – 45.5 GHz band for use around the world.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing for RF Products
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) provides an exciting new method for fabricating parts and assemblies. Structures can be fabricated that are impractical with traditional machining and bonding techniques. Opportunities exist for dramatic cost reductions with significantly reduced delivery times. Many components can be printed using readily available and low-cost printers, allowing in-house fabrication. This presentation describes how AM can be used in designing and producing RF sources and components.

articleTitle: Experimental Measurements of Magnetically-Insulated Coaxial Diode's Space-Charge-Limited Electron-Beam Current, a.k.a. Fedosov Current, on the SINUS-6 High-Current Electron-Beam Accelerator at the University of New Mexico
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The experimental measurements of electron beam cur-rent-voltage (I-V) characteristics on the SINUS-6 accelerator are performed by analyzing (i) the electron-beam current produced by explosive emission cathodes of different types in a magnetically-insu-lated coaxial diode (MICD) of the SINUS-6 accelerator, and (ii) an accelerating voltage applied to the cathodes. The direct comparison of experimentally measured I-V characteristics with analytical cal-culations and numerical particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of the MICD of the SINUS-6 accelerator is presented. The results of the comparison are analyzed, and the following steps in this work are discussed.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Multi-Sheet-Beam Backward Wave Oscillator Based on High-order Mode Orthogonal Grating Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A multi-sheet-beam backward wave oscillator (MSB-BWO) based on high-order mode orthogonal grating waveguides (HOM-OGW) is designed and simulated in this paper. Driven by two parallel sheet electron beams with an identical cross section of 0.49 mm × 0.1 mm and a total beam current of 1.2 A, the beam-wave interaction simulations predicted that a stable radiation power of 280–343 W is obtained across a wide tunable bandwidth of 25 GHz (329–354 GHz).

articleTitle: Diagnostics System for Electron Beam Emission Characteristics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The performance of an electron gun is the most important factor in determining the performance of vacuum electronic devices. Accordingly, electron beam characteristics such as beam current, beam current distribution, beam radius, and beam trajectory should be analyzed before it is assembled with other components. That beam information is essential because the analysis allows us to estimate a performance of the vacuum electronic devices more precisely. We present a simple electron beam diagnostics system to achieve desired beam information and several measured data from the system.

articleTitle: X-band Relativistic Traveling Wave Amplifier*
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A high-power X-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) amplifier was designed and studied using numerical simulations. A sinusoidal corrugated circular waveguide is used as the slow wave structure (SWS) for wave interaction with a 450 kV, 1 kA annular electron beam. From Pierce's theory, the predicted gain at 10 GHz is 1.4 dB/cm with an instantaneous bandwidth of 5% for the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode. A broadband amplifier has the frequency agility necessary to maximize electromagnetic (EM) coupling into targeted electronics. The Input/output microwave coupling is an important factor for an efficient operation. The first stage of this study is to design an input coupler that is compatible with the two electron beams diode, which will be used as a driver. The relativistic TWT was studied using MAGIC Particle-in-Cell (PIC) simulations.

articleTitle: Mode Selectivity of Cylindrical Cavities with Irregular Corrugation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present the results of theoretical studies on mode selectivity of a cylindrical cavity with irregularly corrugated wall for high-power sub-THz and THz gyrotrons. The corrugation is formed by the longitudinal slots, which are positioned with an azimuthal period <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi/m$</tex> in order to discriminate the modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{x\neq m,y}$</tex>. The slots have different height selected according to primitive root sequences. The corrugation introduces additional surface losses and provides strong scattering of the undesired modes. The selectivity of a gyrotron cavity with the proposed structure has been demonstrated by suppression of the fundamental <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{2.3}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{0.3}$</tex> modes and keeping a structure of the second-harmonic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{10.3}$</tex> mode unperturbed.

articleTitle: Enhanced Peak Power Saturation for Impulse Amplification in a Broadband Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present our current progress on exploring broadband impulse amplification in a helix traveling wave tube (TWT) amplifier. Specifically, we have examined the response of a broadband TWT to bipolar differentiated Gaussian impulses and simulated the characteristics of the amplification in a large signal regime. Our simulations predict that the saturated gain of a bipolar differentiated Gaussian impulse input exceeds the saturated gain of single-tone sinusoidal input signals, consistent with previous findings. Additionally, we have simulated the effect of beam energy on the saturated gain of bipolar differentiated Gaussian input impulses. The results show that the saturated peak gain for the Gaussian bipolar impulse is constant (within 1 dB) for a beam energy variation of ±8%, corresponding to a beam velocity variation of ±4% of the nominal design value.

articleTitle: Advances in Scandate Cathode
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper reviewed recent results on scandate cathode developed in our group, especially on the surface analysis of cathode surface and the role of active substance in the cathode. We confirmed the formation of Ba-Sc-O active layer on the scandate cathode by high temperature in-situ TEM observation.

articleTitle: Beam Wave Interaction Studies of Harmonically Related Axially Partitioned Dual Band MILO
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This article deals with the design and beam wave interaction studies of the harmonically related axially partitioned dual band magnetically insulated Line Oscillator (HDBMILO), a cross field type, high power microwave source. The device incorporates a coaxial disc loaded type smooth slow wave structure (SWS) sections separated axially for S-band and X-bands. The interaction SWS region dimensions are conferred through Eigen-mode analysis. Later, the device parameters are optimized through the beam wave interaction studies. At beam voltages 505kV and device currents 47kA, the proposed structure able to generate an HPM RF power of ∼3.9 GW oscillating at 3.5GHz and 10.5GHz, harmonically related, concurrently. The peak conversion efficiency is around ∼16.5%.

articleTitle: Research on TWT Gain Measurement Using Vector Network Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The influences of travelling wave tube (TWT) gain fluctuation caused by input power precision were analyzed, and the main errors of the vector network analyzer source power fluctuation were discussed. Based on the three level control modes, which are internal leveling, power calibration and receiver leveling, the source power variations of vector network analyzer were tested, the results show that the receiver leveling is more efficient and feasible for TWT.

articleTitle: Review and Development of 170 GHz Gyrotron for Nuclear Fusion in BVERI
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper present a series of 170 GHz gyrotron development of Beijing Vacuum Electronics Research Industrial (BVERI). The performance of MW-class high power has been demonstrated at the 170 GHz frequency point by optimizing design scheme and manufacturing 3 versions of gyrotron since 2017. The ongoing improvements of longer operating pulse length and better radiation performance also be described in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of An E-Band Planar Slow-Wave Structure with Energy Transmission Window
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this paper, an E-band planar slow wave structure based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP) and the energy coupling window are designed and analyzed. By adopting the planar structure of SSPP, the slow wave structure has shown good transmission performance and miniaturized size. Meanwhile, with the waveguide-probe transition structure, the energy can be effectively coupled between the waveguide transmission line and the planar microstrip structure.

articleTitle: Operation of Non-Incandescent Cathode in X-Band Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We report a study of operation of non-incandescent cathode of X-band magnetron, which employs field electron emission thin foil sharp blade-type sources to instigate the primary emission of electrons. Conditions and practical considerations necessary to provide stable operation of the cathode are discussed.

Author Keywords: thin foil sharp blade field emitter

articleTitle: Automatic Optimization of Static Electron Beam of Traveling Wave Tube with MFS and EOS
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The periodic permanent magnet (PPM) focusing system is an important part of the traveling wave tube (TWT), which is used to focus the electron beams to pass through the beam wave interaction region stably. However, PPM field optimization is time-consuming, and the optimization results are closely dependent on the designer's experience. The automatic optimization method introduced in this paper, which combines magnetic focusing simulator (MFS) and Electron optics simulator (EOS) to calculate PPM and electron gun, can greatly improve the design efficiency, and the example has shown good performance.

articleTitle: Dispersion Model of a Rectangular, Sinusoidally Corrugated, 220 GHz Backward-Wave Oscillator (BWO)
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper describes the electromagnetic analysis of a rectangular, sinusoidally corrugated, backward wave oscillator (BWO) designed to operate in the low THz regime - ideally operating at 220 GHz. Of interest are the dispersion curves for the first few modes that will propagate through the device. Focus will be placed in analysis and “cold” simulation without the presence of an electron beam. Consideration of propagating modes and field enhancements are taken into consideration, as well as necessary conditions for the electron beam to have adequate resonance at desirable frequencies. These findings will establish the electron beam requirements for such a device and provide a foundation for particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation modeling of the device with beam-wave interaction.

articleTitle: Grating-Groove-Ladder Slow Wave Structure for W-Band Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel slow wave structure (SWS) named grating-groove-ladder (GGL) SWS, is presented to expand the bandwidth of the conventional ladder (CL) SWS. The transmission path of GGL could be modulated by alternately changing the width of the grating on the cover plates. High-frequency results indicate that GGL exhibits a wider bandwidth and improved dispersion characteristics. Meanwhile, GGL shows excellent interaction impedance and ohmic losses. Simulation results verify the broadband transmission characteristics of GGLTWT in the W-band.

articleTitle: A 220 GHz Wideband TWT With Output Power Over 20 W and Bandwidth Over 20 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A 220 GHz wideband traveling wave tube (TWT) has been developed by Beijing Vacuum Electronics Research Institute (BVERI). The TWT is capable of achieving 20 W output power in a 22 GHz bandwidth and 10 W output power in a 36 GHz bandwidth. The maximum output power is 24.5 W @ 220 GHz, and -3 dB bandwidth reaches 34 GHz (15 % of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>). The gain of the TWT is greater than 32.8 dB, and a two-stage deep depressed collector is employed to achieve the efficiency exceeding 7 %. The beam transmission ratio is 90 %, and the maximum stable duty cycle is 10 %.

articleTitle: Development of 150 W, Ka Band TWT for Payload Data Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A Ka-band helix Travelling Wave Tube (TWT),named ET3706, delivering 150 W RF power, continuouswave (CW), at 32 GHz has been developed at LeonardoPalermo Plant under ESA contract n°4000130150/20/NL/HK. The TWT Elegant Breadboard(EBB) has been designed for payload of the Envisionmission high-rate data transmission. Even if the EBB modelis intended for laboratory environment operation, thedevelopment activities have been carried on with attention tothe main electrical and mechanical characteristics in moresever environment such as operation under ThermalVacuum Chamber (TVAC), vibration and shock conditions.It has been made large use of electrical simulations, thermal-stress and mechanical analysis, in order to satisfy the marginof safety coefficients according to European Cooperation forSpace Standardization (ECSS).

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of the Sheet Beam Electron Gun for 0.14 THz SDV-TWT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper narrates the design and measurement of a sheet electron gun for a 0.14 THz staggered double vane traveling wave tube (SDV-TWT). The sheet electron gun was modeled in CST and obtained the expected simulation results. The hot test results display the designed electron gun can satisfy the requirements of the TWT.

Author Keywords: Staggered double vane traveling wave tube (SDV- TWT)

articleTitle: Benchmarking of the SLAC 75XP4, a 75 MW X-band PPM Klystron Brandon Weatherford, Erik Jongewaard, Valery Dolgashev, Don Geranen, Andy Haase
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The SLAC 75XP series klystron was developed in the late nineties / early 2000‘s as a 60% efficient, 75 MW permanent magnet-focused klystron at X-band for the Next Linear Collider (NLC). In 2023, SLAC is resurrecting the 75XP series for potential deployment in future science facilities like the Cool Copper Collider. Here, we discuss the history and lessons learned from the initial 75XP klystrons (75XP1 through 75XP3 series). Finally, an overview of SLAC's current efforts to finish the design, build, and test of an improved 75XP4 version will be presented.

articleTitle: Field Emitter Failure Mechanisms and Harsh Environment Robustness Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Modern day field emitters can fail due to several mechanisms that are not well understood. This paper presents experiments that aim to identify the mechanisms behind failure. Two types of devices, Silicon gated field emitter arrays (SiGFEAs) and Titanium Silicon Oxy Nitride (TiSiON) lateral field emitter devices were characterized experimentally. Si-GFEAs were tested for arc occurrence time for a fixed gate voltage of 50 V and a fixed collector voltage of 200 V. The emitter was grounded. Initial results from the temporal response experiment show that the emitter experiences arcing first. However, future experiments will provide an accurate identification of the arc initiating electrode. For the planar device, a diode was chosen and IV characterization was performed at 50 °C and 400 °C. Experiments showed that for an applied collector voltage of 10 V, the field emission current was ≈ 5.5 nA before the heat treatment and was ≈ 2.75 nA after the 400 °C heat treatment. This reduction in current could be attributed to the removal of water vapor by heat treatment resulting in the reduction in the surface leakage current.

articleTitle: Performance Limits of Electrostatically Controllable Negative Electron Affinity Photoemitters
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Negative electron affinity (NEA) surfaces allow high quantum efficiency photoemission from semiconductors. However, traditional NEA cathodes are only stable under ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) conditions with limited operational lifetime, adding difficulty to manufacturing process. In stark contrast, a semiconductor/insulator/graphene (SIG) heterostructure can generate an NEA surface through an electrostatic bias while showing excellent stability even at atmospheric pressures with a modest external quantum efficiency of 0.1%. Here, we have theoretically studied the performance of a hot electron laser assisted cathode (HELAC) operating with a SIG based NEA surface and identify the key limitations of this device as well as provide an experimental roadmap to reaching the theoretical performance limits.

articleTitle: Simulated and Experimental Oscillation Thresholds of the Recirculating Planar Crossed-Field Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The Recirculating Planar Crossed-Field Amplifier (RPCFA) is a high power microwave amplifier. The RPCFA is initially zero drive stable and exhibits 11.6 dB gain with a 400 kW, 3.05 GHz input signal. By changing the AK gap, the RPCFA acts as an oscillator or a driven oscillator when an input signal is present. The experimental and simulated operating parameters and microwave output characteristics will be discussed.

articleTitle: The Nature and Distribution of Materials at the Emitting Surface and Throughout the Thickness of High-Performance Scandate Cathodes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Scandate cathodes offers promise of significant improvements in electron gun performance but are still hindered by two interrelated issues. It is not yet known which processing approach(es) would effectively guarantee strong device performance, and there are remaining questions as to the exact nature and preferred location of the materials and phases that should exist throughout a well-functioning scandate cathode. This study focused on the latter aspect, by providing a detailed understanding of the materials at the emitting surface as well as a more global view of the materials distribution throughout the cathode pellet. Application of advanced specimen preparation methods in combination with detailed materials characterization techniques facilitated a comprehensive understanding of the material phases in scandate cathodes. This study also points the way toward additional characterization experiments for definitive quantification of the surface materials that most directly influence electron emission.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experiments on the Coaxial, All-Cavity Extraction, Recirculating Planar Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Simulations and experiments were carried out on the coaxial, all-cavity extraction, recirculating planar magnetron (RPM-CACE) which extracts power from adjacent cavities for pi-mode operation. Experimental and simulation data demonstrated that at −300 kV, the design is not operating in the desired pi-mode; thus, the maximum power cannot be extracted efficiently. In simulations, electron spokes did not form in every other cavity, as expected for pi-mode. In the −300 kV experiments, the device began oscillating during the voltage rise, but never reached steady state operation.

articleTitle: Enhancement of a 263 GHz EPR Spectrometer with TWT Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A compact, broadband 263 GHz TWT amplifier is incorporated into a high-field pulse EPR spectrometer system. The pulsed TWT amplifier, with 10 GHz 3-dB bandwidth, operates at 20.25 kV cathode voltage and provides 25.5 dB gain in saturation. A preliminary experiment has been carried out to examine the performance of the implementation. The wideband and moderate power TWT demonstrates a dramatic improvement on the signal intensity of the nano-second pulse sequence from 200 mW to more than 7 W over 5 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Investigation on Multi-Port Radial Extraction S-Band Relativistic Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Investigating the impact of extraction cavities on frequency characteristics is an important task for multi-port RM development. In this paper, the dispersion characteristics and loaded quality factor of A6 RM (Relativistic Magnetron) with different cavities positions and numbers are studied using CST (Computer Simulation Technology) Studio. The results show that the multi-port output of adjacent extraction cavities is beneficial to improve mode isolation, the loaded quality factor decreases and the output power increases with the increase of the number of extraction cavities.

articleTitle: TWT Folded Wave-Guide High-Frequency Losses Test and Simulation Based on Surface Roughness
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This study introduces the W-band and G-band travelling wave tube (TWT) folded wave-guide (FWG) high-frequency losses (HFL) test and simulation. This is a method that does not require adjusting electric conductivity of the material during simulation. We respectively set the FWG E-plane and H-plane roughness based on test data, and then set the electric conductivity as the same with copper used in DC. The HFL simulation results obtained were matched with the test data at 91-101GHz and 195-225GHz. This indicates that the surface roughness of the material is the main source of HFL.

articleTitle: Optimizing the inner diameter of reflector for high-power microwaves generation in multivircator
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this investigation, we developed an axial virtual cathode oscillator (vircator) by introducing a dielectric reflector within the downstream region of the waveguide. The objective was to optimize the inner diameter for the efficient generation of high-power microwaves from a multivircator. The reflector's inner diameter was systematically adjusted to 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 cm. Through comprehensive particle-in-cell simulations, it was noticed that the maximum peak power was achieved when the reflector's inner diameter was set at 2 cm, Moreover, the analysis of the phase space of all electrons reveals a dependency on the inner diameter of the reflector for the formation of the VC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. It is crucial to emphasize that when the inner diameter of the reflector exceeds the diameter of the physical cathode (9 cm), VC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> formation does not occur.

articleTitle: Development of Compact Low-Voltage Klystrons for Integrated Linear Accelerator Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: SLAC is developing multiple compact, lightweight, and portable integrated accelerator systems. Being developed for these systems are integrated modulators, low-level RF controls, linac structures, and RF sources. Advances in each of these technologies has paved a path forward for a fully integrated man-portable linear accelerator system. Due to the size and weight constraint of these systems, relatively low voltage (<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">~</sup>60 kV) X-band and C-band klystrons have been developed. A push towards scalable and cost-effective RF sources has enabled the novel design of multiple compact klystrons. An update on the build and test status of some of these klystrons will be presented in this work.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Field Emission Based Magnetron for Industrial Applications Using 3-D Conformal Finite-Difference Time-Domain Particle-in-Cell Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This work extends our prior investigation of a field emission-based rising-sun magnetron by progressing from 2-D to a comprehensive 3-D conformal finite-difference time domain (CFDTD) particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. Leveraging insights from the 2-D CFDTD PIC simulations, which achieved an efficiency of ~80% with linear anode current density of 75.67 A/m, applied voltage of 5.2 kV, and a static magnetic field of 0.235 T, our 3-D design envisions a rising-sun magnetron with a 10 cm cavity height and an identical cross-sectional area in the x-y plane to achieve similar performance. The cavity optimization process, accounting for geometric and cavity loading effects, converges at an operating frequency of 2.45 GHz. The streamlined fabrication and assembly of the rising-sun magnetron, differing from conventional strapped magnetrons with thermionic cathodes, highlight its practicality and efficiency for industrial applications. This study not only expands insights from 2D simulations but also offers a comprehensive understanding of the potential and feasibility of 3-D design in real-world applications. The shift from 2-D to 3-D strengthens the design, positioning it as a practical alternative to current industrial magnetrons.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis of Metamaterial Absorber Using Finite Element/Boundary Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Metamaterial absorber is a kind of metamaterial that has a great application prospect in electric vacuum devices. In the design of metamaterial absorbers, electromagnetic simulation is a more efficient and cost-effective method. The FEM/BEM combines the advantages of FEM and IE method and especially suitable for the simulation of metamaterial absorbers. In this paper, we developed an electromagnetic simulator based on the domain decomposition based FEM/BEM method for the analysis of metamaterial absorbers. The numerical analysis shows that the simulator is accurate and practicable for simulation of metamaterial absorber.

articleTitle: Analysis of THz Smith-Purcell Radiation in Single- and Two-Layer Gratings Utilizing Hot-Tube Dispersion Relation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR) is generated when an electron beam passes near a periodic structure. The hot-tube dispersion relation is analyzed to compare the spatial growth rates in single- and two-layer gratings. Our analysis reveals that the spatial growth rate, calculated from the hot-tube dispersion relation, is higher for the two-layer structure, resulting in a lower starting current compared to the single-layer grating over a wide range of grating parameters. This observation is further validated through Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulations, providing insights into the enhanced performance of SPR using two-layer grating structures.

articleTitle: 32 GHz Traveling-Wave Tubes Development for Venus Exploration THL32070 and THL32150 Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In the coming years, two exploration missions will target planet Venus. Supported by ESA funding, Thales AVS is participating to these missions by developing two new 32 GHz conduction-cooled traveling wave tubes (TWTs). One delivering 150W RF output power for the EnVision mission, and the second one, 70W for the Veritas mission.

articleTitle: Space-Charge Limited Current for Nonplanar Crossed-Field Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Calculating the space-charge limited current is critical for many applications, such as high-power microwaves, electric thrusters, and nano vacuum transistors. This paper explores the space-charge limited current (SCLC) for a system with a crossed magnetic field in any orthogonal coordinate system. Specifically, we extend prior work using variational calculus to determine SCLC for a cylindrical crossed-field diode and apply capacitance, which has been used for nonmagnetic diodes. These techniques provide less computationally expensive approaches than particle-in-cell codes that may facilitate the incorporation of multiphysics phenomena.

articleTitle: Folded-Waveguide Pulsed Ka-Band TWTs for Earth Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The design of a 400W pulsed-power upper Ka-band TWT with a folded-waveguide delay line intended for earth observation applications is presented, along with measurement results of first prototypes.

articleTitle: Progress and Opportunities in Short-Pulse High-Power Microwave Generation for Compact Particle Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Short-pulse acceleration with nanosecond-long radiofrequency (RF) pulses has been recently explored in particle accelerators research. The nanosecond-long RF pulses were generated using one advanced accelerator concept, structure wakefield acceleration. Experimental studies have demonstrated that the short pulse length could potentially mitigate the impact of RF breakdown, and opened the door for operating accelerators at higher gradients in the short-pulse regime. We envision that complementary approaches in generating short RF pulses is an interesting research topic in the vacuum electronics community.

articleTitle: Graphene-Film Electron Field Emitter for THz VEDs
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: While field electron emitters have seen notable advancements enhancing their applications in diverse fields, challenges such as inconsistent emission, material degradation, and the complexities of nanoscale fabrication persist as significant barriers. This report introduces a graphene electron field emitter as a promising candidate for the sheet- beam electron source for developing compact, high-power terahertz (THz) sources. Since the discovery of graphene, there has been a continuous pursuit to leverage its superior properties by restoring its exceptional characteristics in film or paper forms, often referred to as reduced graphene oxide (rGO). Typically, the material properties of rGO are constrained by the oxidation process, but they can be enhanced limitedly through a general high-temperature annealing process. In this report, a turbostratically stacked 2.5-D graphene film (TGF), fashioned through an innovative binder-free gelation technique, has showcased superior performance in both material and field emission properties. This includes an electrical conductivity of 1.95× 10^6 S.m^-1, electron mobility of 818 cm^2.V^-1.s^-1, thermal conductivity of 2000 W.m^- 1.K^-1, and current exceeding 10 mA with a current density over 300 A.cm^-2. Additionally, the TGF maintained a 10% current degradation after 25 days of continuous DC operation at 1.5 mA. The film used is typically about 300 nm in thickness and 1-2 cm in width. Utilizing this graphene electron field emitter, we are progressing in the development of a THz vacuum electron device.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Design of a 100-kW L-Band lOT Amplifier for Accelerator Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We show recent progress of a high efficiency 100 kWlOT amplifier design operating at 1.3 GHz. The lOT is composed of a multi cavity interaction circuit with upward of 80% power efficiency. We present details of the electrical and thermal design of the lOT as well as testing plans.

articleTitle: Integration of the Magnetic Circuits for Magnetrons Using New Magnetostatic Solvers in VSim
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Magnetic circuit designs are crucial to operations of many vacuum electronics devices, such as magnetrons, klystrons, and traveling wave tubes. For magnetrons, either electromagnets or permanent magnets are used. There are already some commercial software packages on the market for magnetic circuit designs such as Maxwell and COMSOL based on a finite element method (FEM). However, for a full simulation of these devices, one has to export the magnetic circuit design and import it into a particle-in-cell (PIC) code for studying particle-wave interaction as most of these packages are not PIC codes. In this work, we propose to use the magnetostatic solvers newly developed in VSim for conducting the magnetic circuit designs as the same finite difference grids are used, avoiding the troubles caused by an export/import process or additional errors due to a translation/interpolation. To understand the feasibility of employing the magnetostatic solvers, the simulation results are also compared with those from the FEM simulations. The detailed formulation and demonstrations will be presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization and Design of L-band Sheet Beam Electron Gun
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper introduces the design and optimization of an L-band sheet beam electron gun using the in-house automatic optimization program SB_EGUNAPP2.0. The beam voltage is 20 kV and the beam current is 5 A, with compression ratio of 4.8. The simulation results demonstrate that the electron gun produces a sheet beam with the intended beam cross-section at a beam waist position of 53.76 mm from the bottom of cathode.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of an Overmoded V-Band Sapphire Pillbox Window
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper proposed an overmoded pillbox window for high-frequency vacuum electronic devices. A V-band sapphire example was designed, fabricated, and tested to verify the validity of the overmoded pillbox window. The simulation results show that the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of the V-band overmoded pillbox window is lower than 1.4 in the frequency range of 62-70 GHz. 3 samples were successfully fabricated. The experimental results indicate that their VSWR is lower than 1.5 in the frequency range of 62.5-70 GHz and their airtightness is good. For comparison, this paper also fabricated 2 regular V-band sapphire pillbox windows and tested their transmission characteristic. The experimental results verified that the overmoded pillbox windows can hold a larger dielectric disk than the regular ones at the expense of bandwidth.

articleTitle: Thorough Simulation of High-Power Gyrotron Cavity Interaction in the Hard Excitation Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Using the new interaction code Phaedra, a thorough and systematic investigation of the operation of a high-power gyrotron cavity in the hard excitation regime took place. The preliminary result of this analysis shows that in the hard excitation regime, the nominal mode can potentially be excited at more than one frequency with a difference in the range of few tens of MHz and with a significant power difference at the same accelerating voltage. Furthermore, improper choice of parameters for the startup simulations can guide to an important overestimation of the stability of the mode at higher voltages.

articleTitle: The Effect of Space Charge on the Performance of Linear Beam Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Space charge effect is analyzed on beam-cavity interaction by using an example of an inductive output tube (IOT), a high-power amplifier with a high efficiency for RF power amplification. To ensure the reliability and efficiency of electron beam systems, large signal analysis of electron beam interaction requires the consideration of space charge effects as it leads to the dissipation of energy. Space charge effects are investigated using the disk model of IOT to test the device performance and the behavior of normalized velocity and kinetic energy when an electron beam passes through an interaction gap. We observed that space charge increases the kinetic energy which leads to lower conversion efficiency.

articleTitle: Possible Improvement of AM/PM Conversion Induced by Positive Phase Jump in FWG TWT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The increasing demand for communication quality has prompted the exploration of enhancing the linearity of traveling wave tubes (TWTs). However, the implementation processes of some commonly used methods, such as incorporating an external negative feedback circuit, can be intricate. In this article, we preliminarily attempt a novel method of adjusting the electrons' phase called the positive phase jump (PPJ) method, to optimize the amplitude modulation/phase modulation (AM/PM) conversion characteristics of folded waveguide (FWG) traveling wave tubes. This method requires inserting a special structure into the traditional FWG slow wave structure (SWS) that allows for a global positive phase jump experienced by the electron beam. Consequently, electrons can undergo a phase jump after passing through this structure and lag behind the wave. It should be noted that apart from incorporating a PPJ structure, no additional modifications have been made to the remaining components of the slow wave circuit compared to a conventional FWG SWS. After conducting simulation verification on our preliminary design, it has been proven that this approach effectively reduces the absolute values of AM/PM to approximately 6 degrees/dB, without power and efficiency reduced.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Adjoint Methods in the MICHELLE Beam Optics Code
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present progress on the application of an adjoint approach to determine sensitivity functions for the design of charged particle optics in the presence of both electric and magnetic static fields. The methodology is applied by implementing techniques in the MICHELLE beam optics code whereby a minimal number of time-reversed simulations enables the determination of a variety of figures of merit resulting from small, but arbitrary, property changes. Such changes may include geometric electrode shapes, magnetic field patterns, electrode voltages, emission properties, etc. The use of these sensitivity functions to determine manufacturing alignment and assembly tolerances to maximize production yield as well as in optimization algorithms will be discussed. Applications to beam transport in magnetic fields will be presented.

articleTitle: Precision Bead-Pull Test Bench with New Self-Centering Procedure
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present the design and results of a new precision bead-pull test bench. We devised a new self-centering procedure in order to reach high accuracy on the electromagnetic field amplitude, something not within reach with previous benches. Measurement of coupling impedance changes along pitch tapered helices becomes possible, as well as precise RF losses estimate.

articleTitle: Experiment of An Electron Gun for Ku Band Continuous Wave Klystron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Tunable continuous wave klystrons, as the final power amplifiers, are widely used for uplink signal transmission in the satellite earth stations. Electron gun is the core component of the klystron, its stability determines the performance of the whole device. This article presents the design of a high perveance electron optical system for Ku band tunable continuous wave klystron. On this basis, the influence of electron gun structure design on cathode thermal efficiency is discussed, the electron gun sample is presented and the emission test is carried out. In condition of low working ratio pulse, the experimental results show that the pass rate of the electron beam is above 99%, and the pass rate under high frequency signal output state is more than 97.5%. This study has laid an important technical foundation for the development of tunable continuous wave klystrons.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of High-Power Millimetre Wave Drilling Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: After using the 28GHz and 45GHz high-power millimetre wave to radiate basalt and granite, we assess the feasibility of applying high-power millimetre to the drilling industry and analyse the problems that need to be solved based on the effect of the high-power microwave radiation

articleTitle: A Tunable Narrow-band THz Radiation Using Subwavelength Hole Array Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Subwavelength hole array (SHA) structures have attracted significant attentions because of their extraordinary optical transmission characteristic. In this study, we investigate a SHA layer that can control the Smith-Purcell radiation. The results show that the transmission characteristic can narrow the radiation spectrum and make the radiation tunable. Therefore, it can be concluded that the radiation from this kind of composited structure can be simplified by the radiation controlled by a SHA layer, and it provides a fast way to reshape the radiation spectrum by designing the SHA. With the development of micro-nano processing technologies, this structure is expected to develop into an efficient way to produce terahertz radiation.

articleTitle: Extended V-Band Helix TWT for Future High Throughput Satellite Uplink Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: NEC Network and Sensor Systems, Ltd. has developed extended V-band (47.2 - 52.4GHz) 250W peak 150W cw TWT(Traveling-Wave-Tube) with 2-stage collector. This was accomplished with attention to detail in the design of performance and reliability in support of future VHTS(Very High Throughput Satellites) uplink application. This paper presents the summary of this development, which is based on NEC's standard V-band (47.2 - 51.4 GHz) TWT[1].

articleTitle: 55-Watt Ka-Band Linearized Quad-Channel Microwave Power Module for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Stellant Systems (Stellant) and Macom Technology Solutions (Macom) are completing space-flight qualification for a 55-watt saturated (36-watt nominal operating point) Ka-band linearized quad channel microwave power module (QMPM) capable of 3 GHz instantaneous bandwidth ideally suited for phased array applications. This report will discuss the QMPM performance and qualification plan.

articleTitle: Simulated and Measured Scattering Parameters of Self-Winding Helices at Millimeter Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Transmission properties of self-winding helices at millimeter frequencies are investigated by numerical simulations and contact measurements of scattering parameters. A canonical circuit analysis quantifies any impedance mismatch between the simulated and the measured structures.

articleTitle: Non-Ideal Electron Beam Effect on Ka-band Folded Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper presents a folded waveguide slow wave structure for high power traveling wave tube (TWT). The folded waveguide is a rectangular waveguide by bending the groove along the longitudinal direction and operates with a circular electron beam. Conventionally, we designed folded waveguide TWTs to achieve desired performance under ideal conditions in a design stage using various simulation codes, however, its practical performance differs significantly from the predicted one. To improve accuracy of TWT's performance prediction, we used the CST Studio Suite simulation tool to confirm how changes in electron beam information affect the gain of the folded-waveguide TWT. Through this study, we would like to emphasize the importance of electron beam information in the simulation.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a Dual Frequency 70/105 GHz, 600 kW, CW Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Communications & Power Industries (CPI) has completed the detailed design of a dual-frequency gyrotron and matching optics unit capable of producing over 600 kW of continuous RF output at either 70 GHz or 105 GHz, by adjusting operating conditions to excite either the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> or the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</inf>, 5 mode in a cylindrical interaction cavity. Fabrication of two identical gyrotrons and two matching optics units is nearly complete, and factory testing of the first gyrotron is anticipated to begin in the spring of 2024. In this paper, design analyses will be discussed, and preliminary test results, if available, will be presented.

articleTitle: Multipactor Mitigation Using Anharmonic, Quasi-Aperiodic RF Field Via Two-Tone Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We observed two-surface multipactor onset in a 3 mm gap between copper surfaces for a 440.110 MHz, 225 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf> RF electric field. We then added a second tone, at 249.212 MHz, starting at a low intensity, such that we could still detect multipactor. We increased the power gradually and observed partial multipactor suppression with increasing amplitude of the second tone. After increasing the second tone amplitude to 71.1 V pp, we observed indications of full multipactor suppression. We hypothesize that the multipactor suppression is due to selecting the frequency of the second tone such that the combined two tones form a highly irregular (anharmonic) RF waveform that is not periodic for the duration of the measurement.

articleTitle: Review of Development History and Ongoing Development Status of a 100 A Discharge Current Reservoir Hollow Cathode for Electric Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The reservoir cathode was the first “dispenser” cathode predating the impregnated dispenser cathode in common usage today throughout the vacuum electron device community by nearly 5 years. Extremely long processing times necessitated by its use of barium oxide, incorporated. in the reservoir in the form of barium-strontium carbonate, as the source of barium adsorbates for work function lowering made it impractical for use in many applications. Upon introduction of the impregnated dispenser cathode the reservoir cathode was relegated to use only in a very few applications where its unique capabilities, primarily the ability to deliver high current densities and useful life times at operating temperatures substantially in excess of those of which the impregnated version was capable, justified its use. In 2004 the capabilities of the reservoir cathode led to it being recognized as a possible solution to meeting the lifetime and discharge current requirements for the NEXIS ion thruster being developed for use on the Jupiter Icy Moons Orbiter mission. This required development of an entirely different cathode structure and demonstration of the ability to operate as a gas discharge electron source, rather than a vacuum electron source. Development was quickly curtailed due to cancellation of the mission, but sufficient fabrication and testing experience was acquired to demonstrate the viability of the reservoir cathode in the hollow cathode configuration. Starting in 2012 e-beam initiated a program to further the development of the reservoir hollow cathode. The history of the development of the reservoir hollow cathode is reviewed in this paper and the status of current development efforts are reported. Reservoir hollow cathodes have been successfully operated at discharge currents as high as 100 A in low duty pulse operation and work is progressing on test vehicles capable of extending the capability to CW operation.

articleTitle: 100-Watt K/Ka-Wideband Microwave-Power Module for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Stellant Systems, Inc. (Stellant) has completed the first prototype build of an octave-bandwidth K/Ka-band microwave power module with over 10 GHz of instantaneous bandwidth ideally suited for radar applications and threat simulation. This report will discuss the TWT and MPM performance, and future work.

articleTitle: Studies on High Efficiency Ka-Band Space-Borne Extended Interaction Klystron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: To satisfy the space-borne tasks of meteorologic observation, planetary researches, and interferometric imaging, a new trial to develop a high efficiency Ka-band extended interaction klystron (EIK) is put on the agenda. In the high frequency circuit design, it is paid more attention to realizing high efficiency as far as possible; meanwhile, the circuit is kept stable using high lossy bunching cavities. The beam voltage and current are 17 kV and 0.72 A, respectively. The simulated output power is over 3 kW in the bandwidth of >100 MHz, and the maximum efficiency is above 30%. The preliminary test is finished with the beam transmission of 97% and the output power of 2.4 kW.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Space-Charge-Limited Current and Anode Current of Thermionic Emission Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper introduces a method for simulating the space-charge-limited current and thermal cavity anode current of a thermionic cathode emission magnetron using a particle tracking solver. The particle tracking solver enables the simulation and analysis of the space-charge-limited current in the magnetron, which increases with anode voltage. The simulated trends of the space-charge-limited current in the magnetron match closely with experimental and theoretical calculations. Furthermore, by applying a 4 kV electric field, 0.17 T magnetic field, and 2.6 GHz intrinsic mode electric field, a combined simulation determines the thermal cavity anode current of the magnetron in its operational state to be 0.61 A, with particle trajectories resembling the spokes of a π-mode oscillation. This simulation approach provides a method for studying the space-charge-limited current and thermal cavity anode current of magnetrons.

articleTitle: Thales TH1507U 140 GHz 1.5 MW CW Industrial Gyrotron for W7-X ECRH System Upgrade
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The status of the first 140 GHz 1.5 MW CW (1800s) industrial gyrotron unit (TH1507U) manufactured by THALES for the W7-X Stellarator at Greifswald, Germany, is presented in this paper. The design of the industrial tube and the performance achieved are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of a W-Band Traveling Wave Tube to Obstructions
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present progress on both simulated sensitivities to various obstructions as well as experimental measurements of a W-Band TWT structure. All results are presented in terms of scattering parameters.

articleTitle: A Tunable Uniform Magnetic Focusing System for 0.66 THz Traveling Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A tunable uniform magnetic focusing system is proposed for 0.66 THz traveling wave tubes, comprising two large and two small symmetrical rectangular magnets. The magnetic field amplitude can be adjusted by manipulating the position of permanent magnets. As the height of the two large magnets varies from 5 mm to 25 mm, the amplitude ranges from 0.52 T to 0.36 T. The minimum fluctuation is obtained in the designed electron gun (19.3 kV, 15 mA) under 10 mm height. The hot performance of a folded waveguide traveling wave tube (FWG TWT) under the electron optical system conditions is conducted by a PIC solver, resulting in a maximum output power of 1.05 W at 0.66 THz and a 3dB bandwidth of 8 GHz.

articleTitle: A Pencil Beam Electron-Optical System for Teahertz Vacuum Electronic Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The simulation of a terahertz pencil beam electron-optical system (EOS), comprising an electron gun and a uniform magnetic focusing system with operating voltage of 18–20 kV and current of 14-16.5 mA, is reported. The beam current density exceeds 360 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> due to the miniature radius of beam as 35 μm and tunnel as 50 μm, while the cathode surface current density below 3 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Therefore, the magnetic system provides a peak magnetic field strength of approximately 0.6 T to ensure stable transmission over distances exceeding 30mm with transmission efficiency of 100%.

articleTitle: Thermal Stability of Molybdenum and Molybdenum-Rhenium Alloy Processed by Laser Spot Welding
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Molybdenum and Molybdenum-Rhenium alloy are processed by laser spot welding in cathode component. The process parameters were investigated and optimized. The deformation of welding domain after baking and reprocessing treatment was studied. The results shows that the dimensional variation is less than 3μm, via penetration welding at 510A and girth welding at 350A, with the pulse width of 3.5ms and frequency of 4Hz. The prepared cathode components perform favorable thermal stability via optimized processing parameters.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband Double Ridge RF Window for X-Band Sheet Beam TWT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This article presents the design of an X-band double ridge window that can operate within the frequency range of 5.9-12 GHz, 64.4% in relative bandwidth. The application of optimization techniques in CST results in a reflection coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S_{11})$</tex> of less than −20 dB across the transmission bandwidth. The compact structure of the microwave window discussed in this paper offers advantages for the miniaturization of sheet beam traveling wave tube (TWT). Sensitivity analysis has been conducted to address manufacturing tolerances. A deviation of less than 0.5 mm from the designed value of impedance matching thickness and 0.4 mm from the window thickness is considered tolerable.

articleTitle: An Improved Design of Electron-Optical System for 0.34 THz Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Electron beam performance is one of the most critical parameters of traveling wave tubes (TWTs). In this paper, an improved design scheme of 0.34 THz electron-optical system is presented to generate and transport a high-quality electron beam. To achieve fine-tuning of the tiny electron beam, the design uses the electron gun with double control electrode, including an internal control electrode (ICE) and an external control electrode (ECE). And the cathode with planar emission is employed to facilitate processing and fabrication. To input and output high-frequency signals from the circuit, the topology of the high-frequency system and periodic permanent magnet (PPM) focusing system, which benefited from introducing the D-magnet, is reorganized to enhance the beam transmission rate. This design scheme has great potential to improve the performance of TWTs in the terahertz band.

articleTitle: Cyclotron Resonance Interaction of Electron Beam with the Mode of Topological Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We study the application of a topological photonic crystal in a vacuum electron device. The topological photonic crystal waveguide mode interacts with a gyrating electron beam in a DC magnetic field. A cyclotron resonance oscillator is studied at the frequency of about 22 GHz, DC magnetic field of about 0.7 T, beam voltage of 100 kV, and current of up to 0.3 A.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Dielectric-Supported Meander Line Slow-Wave Structure at Q-band
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A dual-beam dielectric-support meander line slow-wave structure (DSML SWS) is proposed for a Q-band traveling wave tube (TWT). High-frequency characteristics of the proposed SWS have been investigated. According to results from particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, this structure can produce 39.1 W of output power at 40 GHz with the input power of 0.16 W. Additionally, it has a 3-dB bandwidth of 10% centered at 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband L-Band TWTs for Satellite Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A broadband high-power L-Band TWT is developed for use in satellite navigation systems. This TWT is intended to replace several narrow-band TWTs, thus significantly reducing the cost of the satellite. The design challenges for this TWT are discussed, particularly those concerning the delay line. The results of a first breadboard are presented, along with the planned improvements for a second breadboard.

articleTitle: Waveguide Slot Antenna and Antenna Array for High-Power Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: An S-band waveguide slot antenna is designed and employed to construct an array antenna. For the array antenna, additional stubs are used to stop the waves between antennas that would deteriorate the gain and efficiency of the array antenna. Compared to the array antenna without stubs, the gain of the array antenna with stubs is 1.15 dB higher, and the aperture efficiency increased by 23%. The power-handling capacity for this array antenna is 0.59 GW.

articleTitle: Design of a Transmission Line for a 263GHz Gyrotron Traveling-Wave Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A transmission line system presented in this paper is an important gyrotron traveling wave amplifier component. The system includes TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> to HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode converters and a multi-period corrugated waveguide. The mode converter has a 97% transmission coefficient and a reflection below -40 dB operating at 243–283 GHz. The designed transmission line can achieve low-loss performance across a wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Solution of Electromagnetic Focusing System Based on Double Scalar Potential Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: MFS is a magnetostatic solver for PPM system simulation which is widely used by TWT designers in China. However, MFS cannot calculate focusing systems containing both soft magnetic materials and coil materials. To extend its function, the double scalar potential method (DSP) is studied and used to solve the magnetic field distribution of the electromagnetic focusing system. An electromagnetic focusing system is simulated and the results are in good agreement with CST.

articleTitle: Design of Fast Optimization Software for Magnetic System
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper proposed a fast optimization software for magnetic system based on MFS, the Magnetic Field Simulator of Microwave Tube Simulator Suite MTSS. The optimization software has two core functions: (1) Given the target system value of the periodic magnetic field, it can quickly optimize the magnetic field and get the single-ring value corresponding to each magnetic steel. (2) Given the single-ring value of each magnetic steel, it can quickly optimize the magnetic field and get the system value of the corresponding periodic magnetic field. The software is capable of adjusting magnetic system during the actual manufacturing process. Simultaneously, it establishes a seamless connection between magnetic system design and manufacturing, significantly reducing the design and manufacturing cycle of TWT.

articleTitle: Staggered Microstrip Grating Structure for Sheet-Beam TWTs
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We introduce a simple geometry for slow-wave structures (SWSs) in sheet-beam traveling-wave tubes (TWTs). The staggered microstrip grating SWS is a space harmonic structure with geometry and bandwidth with analogous to the staggered vane SWS commonly used for sheet beam TWTs. The staggered microstrip grating TWT is designed to operate in V-band with a center frequency of 74 GHz and electron beam voltage of 20 kV.

articleTitle: Recent Developments of the 2 MW Coaxial-Cavity Pre-Prototype Gyrotron Towards Multi-Frequency Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper gives a summary about recent activities at KIT regarding multi-frequency operation of the coaxial-cavity pre-prototype gyrotron. First, progress on gyrotron experiments above 200 GHz is discussed. Therefore, the existing 170 GHz design has been modified to achieve > 2 MW RF output power with an interaction efficiency > 35 % at 204 GHz operating in a new 10.5 T SC magnet. Second, research is ongoing to improve the cavity mode series for multi-frequency operation satisfying today's and future gyrotron requirements. Here, a new mode series is identified considering improved cavity cooling technology. This mode series shows only a small variation of the caustic radii and has electron beam parameters close to the existing mode series.

articleTitle: Design of an Input Coupler for an X-Band Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The University of New Mexico (UNM) is working on developing a multi-stream Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) amplifier [1], [2]. One of the first steps in the design of a TWT amplifier is to design an input coupler to couple power from a High Power Microwave (HPM) seed source to the slow wave structure (SWS) of the amplifier. In order to aid in the development of a TWT which operates in X-band, multiple options for input couplers have been designed for use in a greater TWT project. This presentation will present the latest efforts made towards designing the input coupler and SWS of the TWT amplifier. The presentation will mainly discuss “cold” structure test results obtained in HFSS simulations.

articleTitle: Optimization and Measurement of an Orthomode Input Coupling System for W-Band Gyro-Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The design and optimization of a W-band ortho-mode input coupling system are reported. The goal was to achieve a reflection under −15 dB over 90–100 G Hz frequency range with minimal transmission loss. The orthomode transducer (OMT) system included a pillbox vacuum window, a 3-dB power splitter, a four-port multi-arm coupler with compact loads on the two return ports and a distributed reflector. Optimized simulations showed better than −20 dB reflection, transmission through one port of −3.1 dB and 12 GHz bandwidth. An OMT with a cavity-type reflector was manufactured and measured. The agreement between simulations and measurement was excellent with a 0.4 GHz frequency shift in the frequency band.

articleTitle: Particle-in-Cell Simulation and Experimental Setup of a Crossed-Field Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A 925 MHz, slow wave meander line crossed-field amplifier (CF A) structure was designed and developed using CST Microwave Studio. The structure has a phase velocity retardation of 24. The high frequency solver shows that the structure has a S11 of −40 dB at 925 MHz. For the PIC simulation, an already developed crossed field structure was used which includes a sole, a segmented collector, two end hats, and an injected electron source. PIC simulation shows that for a sole voltage of −3k V, a magnetic field of 150 G, an injected current of 150 mA, and an RF input power of 15 W, the gain of the structure was 10 dB. Also, experimental studies with a previously developed CF A structure are ongoing. This CF A structure was designed to operate at 600 MHz. An injected beam current of up to 60 mA using gated field emission arrays in an 8 die configuration has been tested. However, no gain was observed so far. Further experiments will be carried out using a higher injected beam current.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Beam Optics Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Calabazas Creek Research, Inc. continues to maintain and upgrade our 3D, charged particle code, Beam Optics Analyzer. We will present several simulation results for actual devices, including heating of a target by backscattered electrons, long pulse particle transport in an electron gun, and a high efficiency multiple beam klystron,

articleTitle: Calculation of Eddy Current Field by Finite Element Method in MFS
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The traveling wave tube focusing system is used to control the electron beam to ensure good passability throughout the entire interaction process. The simulation of most existing focusing systems is still in the stage of static magnetic field simulation without considering eddy current effects. This article studies the calculation method of eddy current field and is for the development of the magnetic field simulator MFS.

articleTitle: Study of Large Orbit Gyro-TWT Window at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper presents a large orbit gyro-TWT window in TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> mode at Ka-band, the double disk window is designed by transmission cascade matrix through the field matching theory. The results of theoretical calculation, simulation and cold-test are consistent. The bandwidth of the window under the condition of the VSWR below 1.3 is 4GHz.
