Thermal analysis shows that when the average power of gyro-TWT is 10kW, the maximum central temperature of the window is 54.186°C and the critical temperature difference is 29.525°C, which concludes the power capacity is 50kW.

articleTitle: Multipactor Analysis of Dielectric-Loaded Parallel Plates with Local-Regional Increment of Secondary Emission Yield
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Multipactor effect is an undesired avalanche-like breakdown in powerful microwave devices, where the presence of dielectric material inevitably forms charge accumulation and accordingly leads to complicated dynamic evolution. Meanwhile, local-regional increment of secondary emission yield (SEY) is probably exacerbated by unexpected surface contamination or different surface roughness, especially for dielectric layers that are hard to polish at fabrication. In this research, the multipactor formation process in dielectric-loaded parallel plates with spatial SEY discrepancy on dielectric surface is investigated with 3D EM-PIC simulation. As revealed in the results, opposite charge polarity eventually forms in the high-SEY region on the dielectric surface, which fully dominates multipactor dynamic evolution as the region size increases.

articleTitle: Electropolishing Additively Manufactured RF Components: An Investigation into Aluminum Texture and RF Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Enhanced losses due to unfavorable surface texture represents a limitation for additive manufacturing of RF components. Precise internal volume finishing methods which can improve performance are needed. This study investigates the impact of electropolishing 3D-printed aluminum, including conventional, high-silicon AlSi10Mg and Al-1Fe-1Zr alloys. Parameters such as bath solution, polishing voltage, time and temperature are systematically analyzed. Obtained surfaces are characterized in term of surface roughness, microstructure and 6GHz surface resistance. The effect of tuned print parameters, alloy composition, sub-surface porosity and final surface roughness is presented. The aim of the present work is to corelate obtained surface properties after electropolishing and RF performances.

articleTitle: ML-Based Analysis of In-Situ Backscatter Electron Detection for Quality Assurance During Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper explores using Additive Manufacturing (AM), specifically Electron Beam Powder Bed Fusion (EB-PBF), to enhance the efficiency of designing vacuum electronic devices (VEDs). While highlighting achievements in copper VED production, we address challenges in the certification process due to the presence of defects. We discuss in-situ techniques using a Total Electron Emissions (TEE) sensor array and machine learning during EB-PBF for real-time VED qualification, aiming to overcome the limitations of post-fabrication evaluation methods.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic PIC Simulation of High Power Microwave Sources using Neptune
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: We present new capabilities in the Neptune electromagnetic particle-in-cell (EM-PIC) simulation code and design environment that support geometry-based design of vacuum electronic and HPM devices. New features of the EM-PIC model include a fully 3D, omnidirectional implementation of the perfectly-matched layer (PML) method that efficiently absorbs outgoing waves, a waveguide port model with time-dependent mode-decomposition diagnostics, and a model for space-charge limited emission from curved (cut-cell) interior surfaces that exhibits second-order convergence of the emitted current density with respect to the grid cell size. Collectively, these capabilities have enabled Neptune to perform 3D simulations of advanced HPM sources. We will summarize the new capabilities and present examples of applications to high power microwave sources.

articleTitle: A New Strategy to Fabricate Sapphire Meta-surface Output Window at Ku-band with Glass Tnterlayer
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A new strategy for the fabrication of Ku-band meta-surface output window was proposed using a glass braze interlayer, to overcome the processing difficulty of the complex sapphire meta-surface window. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Bi}_2 \mathbf{O}_3-\mathbf{B}_2 \mathbf{O}_3-\mathbf{ZnO}-\mathbf{SiO}_2$</tex> glass was prepared with matching thermal expansion coefficient. The reflection of output window in TE01 mode among the Ku- band circular waveguide system was simulated, with a bandwidth of 3.5 GHz below −20dB. The glass filler makes no difference on the performance of meta-surface window. Additionally, the thermal analysis indicates that the output window can withstand up to 150 KW of power.

articleTitle: A Predictive Regression Model for High Frequency Structures in MTSS
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this paper, a predictive regression model for high frequency structure of helix traveling wave tubes is proposed and integrated in MTSS. In the predictive regression model, a double interpolation model is programmed to calculate the characteristics for high frequency structures with certain helix pitch and helix inner radius. XGBoost is trained to establish the forward mapping relationship between the helix pitch, the helix inner radius and the high frequency characteristic parameters. With the predictive regression model, the phase velocity, the coupling impedance and the attenuation constant of helical slow wave structure with changing helix pitch and helix inner radius can be predicted quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Research on Mesh Generation Technology Based on Delaunay Triangulation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: With advancements in computer technology, modeling and simulation have become increasingly important in reducing development costs and enhancing performance. And the core of simulation is mesh generation, the first and most fundamental step in numerical computations. In this paper, utilizing the Delaunay triangulation method, we've developed a three-dimensional mesh generator for microwave tube structures, for significantly enhancing mesh quality and stability. Additionally, the mesh optimization algorithm based on Quasi-Newton method effectively refines poor-quality meshes, a crucial step towards ensuring a numerical simulation reliability under various operational conditions. The numerical results have shown the success of the implemented mesh optimization algorithm, particularly in significantly improving the quality of poor-quality mesh elements. This mesh generator will be incorporated as a core component of Microwave Tube Simulator Suite.

articleTitle: Research on Brazing Technology and Properties of Electron Beam Window
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Electron beam windows are prepared by vacuum brazing. The microstructure, vacuum variables, internal ultra-high vacuum degree and leakage rates of the electronic beam windows were studied by the golden display microscope, the laser displacement sensor, and the ultra -high vacuum baking exhaust system. The results of the study show that the interface of the electron beam window connector is well connected, the thickness is uniform, the welds are not cracking and no other defects are produced In a low vacuum, the deformation of electron beam window is 2.3mm. The titanium membrane welded window with a thickness of 0.1mm can withstand the atmospheric pressure greater than 2.2MPa. After baking and exhaust at 120 °C, the internal ultra-high vacuum degree of the electron beam window is better than 4.59 X10-8pa, and the leakage rate is better than 3.4 X10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−10</sup>Pa.m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/s.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electron Beam Laminar Properties in Helix TWT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The relationship between transverse velocity and transverse position of electron and the electron beam distribution in the helix TWT is analyzed. The gain of helix TWT is simulated by changing the angle spread of particle source under different laminar state of electron beam. The results show that the RMS-emittance can be used to quantify the laminar properties of electron beam in the helix TWT.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Noise Generation in a Re-Entrant Crossed-Field Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Particle-in-cell simulations are used to showcase the transit wobble in electron spokes observed in areentrant crossed-field amplifier (CFA). The transit wobble period corresponds to the time for a spoke to transit 360o• This introduces a strong frequency component readily observable within the spoke, but not on the output signal. While the effects on the output are relatively unclear, a correlation between transit wobble and prominent side-bands is identified. The separation of the prominent side-bands from the operation frequency is often a harmonic of a sub-harmonic of the transit wobble frequency. This observation is important because it indicates possible avenues to reduce side-bands, such as designing CFAs to encourage a purely sinusoidal wobble to minimize sub-harmonics.

articleTitle: Design of Electron-Optical System for 1.03THz Backward Wave Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In This paper, the simulation design of an electron-optical system (EOS) for a 1.03 THz backward wave oscillator (BWO) is presented. The simulation results show that at the operating voltage of 25kV, the current transmitted in the beam tunnel with radius of 0.025mm is 15mA, which can be focused by a 1.29 Tesla permanent magnetic focusing system.

articleTitle: Investigations of Two-Dimensional Brillouin Flow Through a Cylindrical Step Discontinuity
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Two-dimensional Brillouin flow is studied via simulation of a coaxial crossed-field diode. We find that a change in the anode radius introduces novel bunching of the electrons within the Brillouin hub. This bunching occurs at low frequencies, and is much more pronounced if the Brillouin flow is from the small gap region to the large gap region, than if the Brillouin flow is from the large gap region to the small gap region.

articleTitle: Advanced Gyrotrons for Fusion Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Improved gyrotrons will be required for future fusion power plants. These gyrotrons must operate at efficiencies significantly higher than current gyrotrons, and the output must be in HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> waveguide, rather than a Gaussian beam. This research is developing a gyrotron with an efficiency approaching or exceeding 70% with the output in corrugated waveguide.

articleTitle: Memory Effects in Digital Predistortion of TWTAs
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The application of digital predistortion(DPD) to traveling wave tube amplifier(TWTA) can effectively improve linearity, and behavior model including memory effect can solve the model accuracy problem caused by memory effect, but there are few studies on the source of memory effect of TWTA. Based on the research of the memory effect of solid-state amplifier, this paper explores the sources of thermal memory effect and electrical memory effect of TWTA, and proposes a method to characterize the memory effect by the hot standing wave variation of TWTA. The test results show that the strong memory effect occurs when the peak-to-average ratio (PAPR) is greater than 8dB of OFDM signal excitation.

articleTitle: The Study of Electromagnetic Finite Element Method and Bayesian Deep Learning for SWS Analysis Based on Python Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this paper, Python programming is employed to study the electromagnetic finite element method (FEM) and Bayesian deep learning. Rectangular cavity and folded waveguide (FWG) slow-wave structure (SWS) are taken as examples. Compared with the theoretical calculation and HFSS simulation, Python-based FEM (Py_FEM) has considerable calculation accuracy. Additionally, multi- process computing is studied to parallelize the calculation process to reduce the computational time, and adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) is studied to enhance the calculation accuracy. Finally, based on the Py_FEM, a Bayesian neural network (BNN) is trained to provide the prediction value and prediction uncertainty of the dispersion characteristics.

articleTitle: Mechanical-Electromagnetic Coupling Simulation of Microwave Tubes Based on Dynamic Mesh Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Small mechanical perturbations can potentially alter the electromagnetic properties of microwave tubes. It is imperative to consider the impact of displacement deformation on these properties, as it can alter the electromagnetic boundary conditions and the location of the medium computational domain. The structure displacement deformation is crucial to the performance analysis of microwave tubes. This paper introduces a multi-physics simulator system, which is developed using an integrated framework and facilitates mechanical-electromagnetic coupling simulation. Utilizing dynamic mesh technology, the finite element model of the mechanical and electromagnetic computational domains can be automatically updated. Consequently, the electromagnetic computational domain can reflect displacement deformation post-mechanical analysis, eliminating the need for designer intervention. Numerical results indicate that the technology proposed herein can perform mechanical-electromagnetic coupling analysis and accurately depict the actual physical characteristics.

articleTitle: Effects of a Series Resistor on Quantum Tunneling Current in Dissimilar Metal-Insulator-Metal Nanogap
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This study presents current-voltage (1-V) characteristics to show the series resistor's impact on the tunneling current of dissimilar metal-insulator-metal nanoscale junctions by using a self-consistent quantum model in a lumped circuit. As the resistor increases, the current becomes predominantly determined by the series resistor rather than the nano-junction 's properties.

articleTitle: Design of an Overmoded X-band MILO
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Preliminary design of an X-band magnetically insulated line oscillator was performed based on analytical solutions for Brillouin flow, followed by simulation in ANSYS High Frequency Simulation Software (ANSYS-HFSS), and CST Particle Studio (CST-PS). At X-band frequencies, the device dimensions become quite small, and RF breakdown is a concern. To increase feature sizes and mitigate this, a large radius overmoded slow wave structure (SWS) was designed and simulated. In simulation, when driven by a -300 kV pulse, the MILO generated a ~10 kA electron beam and operated in the HEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode, producing 34 MW at 8.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Design Method for Interaction Circuit of High Efficiency Helix TWTs
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: In this paper, a design method for the interaction circuit of high efficiency helix traveling-wave tubes (TWTs) is presented. By observing the change of field relative phase, the method can quickly get a design scheme of the interaction circuit with phase-velocity tapering. The design steps are characterized in the paper, which has been revised by the engineering experience. The interaction circuit of a C-band helix TWT is designed by using this method, the output power and electronic efficiency are more than 120W and 25%, respectively.

articleTitle: Characterization of Nanocomposite Scandia Tungstate Electron Emitter Surface Though Algorithm Assisted Statistical Analysis of Boundaries
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper describes a methodology for assessing the uniformity of the emissive surface of Nanocomposite Scandate Tungsten electron emitters. The approach applies the watershed segmentation algorithm to scanning electron microscope images of an emitter to identify boundaries between tungsten crystallites and the porous space between them. The mapped image is statistically modeled and a framework for consistent evaluation of emitter surface quality is produced.

articleTitle: A 50 Watt Ka-Band Mini Traveling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper describes RF performance on a Ka-broadband mini TWT, which designed for use in a compact MPM. An output power of greater than 50W has been demonstrated across 26.5 GHz to 40GHz, and the efficiency is more than 40%.

articleTitle: Concept of a Nested Cavities Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The authors propose the concept of a two-beam gyrotron with an original electrodynamic system, which consists of coaxially nested cavities. From an applied point of view, such a system can be used, e.g., for simultaneous generation of microwave radiation at two frequencies with significant powers. Dual-frequency plasma heating is of interest for ECR ion sources with improved characteristics. An example of the design of such a cavity is given, which provides simultaneous generation of 28 GHz and 14 GHz with powers of several kilowatts. At the same time the proposed scheme allows to switch between two arbitrary frequencies with appropriate tuning of the magnetic field.

articleTitle: A Multi-SWS Hybrid High-Frequency Circuit for 0.66 THz TWTs
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A hybrid high-frequency circuit consisting of both folded waveguide (FWG) and extended beam tunnel folded waveguide (EFWG) slow wave structures (SWSs) is proposed. Optimizing the proportion of FWG SWS and EFWG SWS in the entire circuit shows the potential to overcome the challenges presented by single-type circuits for their output power, gain, and circuit length. Driven by a pencil beam of 19.2kV, 15.0mA, and an input power of 1 mW, the output performances of the hybrid circuit and single-type circuits are evaluated using the particle-in-cell (PIC) method. Compared with the pure FWG circuit, the saturated hybrid circuit length demonstrates a 37.5% reduction. Compared with the pure EFWG circuit, the output power has a 63.7% improvement and gets a 25.0% broadening of the 3-dB bandwidth.

articleTitle: Advances in Linearizers for TWTAs in Space
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: For power amplifiers (PAs) used in space the prime need is lower dc power. Today linearized TWTAs (LTWTAs) provide the best way to minimize dc power; and new highly efficient miniature TWTAs (also known Microwave power modules, MPMs) can provide the most compact PAs essential for new space applications. Recent Versatile Linearizers (VLs) enable TWTAs to provide optimum efficiency over a wide range of power levels (> 6 dB dynamic range), frequency (> 100 GHz) and bandwidth (> 3 GHz). These PAs are ideal for phased array and shaped, multibeam applications.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of 76 GHz Spatially Harmonic Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A compact and efficient source is required to explore the potential of millimeter wave (MMW) frequencies. A high-power MMW magnetron has been developed to serve in medical imaging, nondestructive testing, and RADAR applications. The design methodology has been developed using the Eigenmode and BH curve analysis. The Particle-in-Cell (PIC) simulation of MMW magnetron predicts the RF power of 20kW at 76 GHz with an efficiency of 6.67%.

articleTitle: Study of Ionized Particles in a Gyrotron Using a Full Gyrotron Simulation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: The ionization of the residual gas in gyrotrons causes the generation of positively charged ions and negatively charged electrons. Using the electron optics code Ariadne, it was possible to simulate the behavior of these electrons in the overall gyrotron geometry in the presence of static electric and magnetic fields as well as the electromagnetic field of the nominal transverse electric mode in the cavity. The main observation of this study is that the negatively charged electrons gain enough energy from their passage through the cavity to overcome the decelerating voltage and escape towards the collector. On the other hand, the positively charged ions remain trapped in the cavity region contributing to the neutralization effect.

articleTitle: A Simple Space Charge Limited Emission Algorithm for 1-D Particle-in-Cell Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Most vacuum electronic devices (VEDs) have cathode emission operating in a space-charge limited regime, indicating that the self-field of space charges limits the current density that can be drawn. In particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, implementing space charge-limited emission can be nontrivial and may generate over-emission or nonphysical effects. In this work, we present a simple algorithm applying the Child-Langmuir law at the first grid instead of attempting to zero the field at the surface, making the algorithm particularly well suited to the PIC simulations. To demonstrate this, a space charge limited (SCL) diode, where the steady-state limiting current should follow the Child-Langmuir law, is simulated using the 1-D bounded electrostatic PIC code, XPDP1, developed by the Plasma Theory and Simulation Group (PTSG), formerly at UC Berkeley, now at Michigan State University. After implementing the simple SCL algorithm in the XPDP1 code, the surface electric field is computed accurately by applying the Gauss law to the surface grid, and the turn-on of the SCL emission in the planar diode is studied carefully. The simple algorithm can be further implemented in 2-D or 3-D PIC simulations for modeling VEDs with SCL emission. The detailed implementation and simulation results will be presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Design and Whole-Cavity Simulation of a Multiple Beam Inductive Output Tube Using a 3rd Harmonic Drive on the Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: A high efficiency, Multiple Beam Inductive Output Tube (MBIOT) with an efficiency greater than 80% would substantially reduce the operating costs of next-generation particle accelerators. We discuss the development of an MBIOT that employs a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{\text{rd}}$</tex> harmonic drive component on the grid to achieve efficiencies greater than 80%. We discuss a novel input coupler, grid design, and whole-cavity simulation of the output cavity using the NEMESIS code. This presents a path forward to the design and production of such high efficiency MBIOTs.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Molybdenum and Oxygen-free Copper Vacuum Brazed Joints
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: Heterogeneous molybdenum-oxygen-free copper (Mo-OFC) joint was successfully brazed in vacuum with AgCu28 filler. The surface morphology, mechanical properties, and fracture morphology of Mo-OFC joint were systematically investigated. The welded joint of Mo-OFC is smooth and continuous. The average shear strength of Mo-OFC joint is 107. 74 MPa, while brittle fracture occurs on the molybdenum side. The average tensile strength of Mo-OFC joint is 121.64 MPa, while plastic fracture occurs on the copper side.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of the Planar PPM Focusing System for Integrated TWT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper investigates a planar PPM focusing system dedicated to a two-beam by one-dimensional array. The simulation reveals the consistency in the axial and transverse components of the magnetic field in two tunnels along the axis. Two tunnels were meticulously designed and fabricated, and the measured results show that the two-beam array achieves a long-distance transmission rate of over 85 %, respectively. The developed magnet offers an innovative solution for designing a one-dimensional electron beam array in integrated TWTs.

articleTitle: High Current and High Stability Field Emission Carbon Nanotubes Emitters for Cold Cathode Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: High current and high stability carbon nanotubes (CNTs) field emission cathode is studied for application in cold cathode magnetron in this paper. And this cathode was prepared by printing the mixture of CNTs and silver paste. Under impulse excitation the CNTs cold cathode has a high field emission current of 100 mA and good field emission stability when the concentration of CNTs was 8%. This study would be helpful to realize the cold magnetron and the application of cold cathode in other vacuum electronic devices.

articleTitle: Design of Slow-Wave Structures Based on Modulated Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint International Vacuum Electronics Conference and International Vacuum Electron Sources Conference (IVEC + IVESC)
abstract: This paper introduces the design of a planar slow-wave structure (SWS) based on modulated spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP) operating in the W-band. The design capitalizes on the −1th spatial harmonic to efficiently radiate energy. In comparison to traditional planar SSPP SWSs, the proposed design maintains transmission performance while enhancing the longitudinal field distribution within the electron beam transit region.
